The loop unconditionally does `yield next(iter_primary)` and then decrements to_yield. If the longest iterable is empty, or lengths supplied do not match the real iterables, StopIteration is raised instead of terminating gracefully.
Secondary items are yielded with `next(iters_secondary[i])` without a StopIteration guard. A mismatch between supplied lengths and the real iterable, or an empty secondary, will raise StopIteration.
peek always calls `next(self)` which advances the iterator. The peeked value is never put back into the cache for the normal maxlen>0 case, so the item is lost and subsequent iteration skips it.

For maxlen>0 the code sets `self._index = len(self._cache)` when _index is None and then decrements it, which yields -1 for an empty cache and otherwise moves the internal cursor without actually restoring the item consumed by `next(self)`. Repeated peeks will consume items.
tags or sys_tags() treats an explicitly passed empty tags sequence as falsy and falls back to sys_tags(), ignoring the caller’s intent.
environment["python_full_version"] is indexed directly when environment is truthy. If the caller supplies an environment dict without that key a KeyError is raised.
A second select method is defined immediately after the first one, silently overwriting it. The first implementation is dead code and the file contains two conflicting definitions.
The second select implementation repeats the direct environment["python_full_version"] indexing, so the same KeyError can occur when environment is provided without the key.

pypy and graalpy ABI strings are built with '-' joins e.g. 'pypy38-pp73' and 'graalpy-38-native'. The comments document the expected tags with underscores 'pypy38_pp73' / 'graalpy_38_native'; if _normalize_string does not replace dashes the ABI tag is wrong.
sample is assigned to pre_alias/post_alias without a leading space, producing e.g. `tblTABLESAMPLE` when other clauses are empty.
when is appended to table before changes is added, generating `tbl WHEN... CHANGES...` while Snowflake syntax requires `CHANGES` before `AT/BEFORE (when)`.
ROWS FROM overwrites table but return still adds only/changes/partition/file_format/sample/version etc, producing invalid `ROWS FROM (...)` with those clauses.
Return places alias before indexed (`tbl AS t INDEXED BY i`), while SQLite requires INDEXED BY/NOT INDEXED before the alias.
EXTRACT(days FROM interval) returns only the days field, not total days, so WEEK diff is wrong once the interval spans months/years.
QUARTER uses `EXTRACT(month...)/3` then CAST truncates toward zero, giving wrong result for negative differences where floor is needed.
Fallback for unknown unit sets unit to an interval and emits CAST(interval AS BIGINT), which is invalid in Postgres.
INSERT uses PARTITION (...) not PARTITION BY, so matching PARTITION_BY never matches and partition clause is never parsed.
DEFAULT value is built as upper-cased Var instead of a Default/keyword node, producing wrong AST and round-trip SQL.
Wrapping `this` in a new Schema overwrites any column list already parsed by _parse_insert_table.
Guard checks _next instead of _curr, so a single trailing action token is never consumed and parser lookup uses the table name.
Accessing self._prev.token_type assumes _prev exists and crashes when parser is at start or after failed parse.
ensure_list(None) yields [None] so failed _try_parse is not detected and None is appended to actions instead of falling back to Command.
Requiring `not self._curr` falls back to Command on trailing semicolon or any extra token, discarding a valid Alter.

Wheel filenames are parsed by counting '-' characters and splitting with dashes-2. Distribution names may contain '-', so dash count is unreliable and split assigns the wrong parts, causing false InvalidWheelFilename errors or incorrect name/version/build/tag extraction for valid wheels.

Name validation uses _wheel_name_regex.match which can succeed on a prefix. An invalid project name that has a valid prefix followed by illegal characters would be accepted, breaking the contract that raises InvalidWheelFilename for bad names.

env_python_full_version is obtained via environment['python_full_version'] if environment else default. If a non-empty environment dict is supplied without the 'python_full_version' key, a KeyError is raised instead of falling back to default_environment or raising a controlled error.
Exactly-one check uses bool(direct_url.vcs_info)+bool(direct_url.archive_info)+bool(direct_url.dir_info)!=1. If a present info object is falsy, the test incorrectly rejects a valid DirectUrl.
env_python_full_version accesses environment['python_full_version'] without checking key existence, raising KeyError when an environment dict is supplied but lacks that key.
The duplicated select implementation repeats the same KeyError for python_full_version when environment is provided without the key.
create_compatible_tags_selector(tags or sys_tags()) treats an empty tags sequence as falsy and falls back to sys_tags(), changing caller intent.
select is defined twice in the same class; the first definition is dead code and differs from the second in tag handling, causing inconsistency and confusion.
Raising with `from defect` chains a non-BaseException object. `defect` is an email.policy.Defect, so `raise ... from defect` raises TypeError at runtime when a header defect is present.
Charset comparison is case-sensitive. RFC 2045 charset names are case-insensitive, so 'utf-8' is rejected even though it is valid.
Markdown variant is compared case-sensitively against {'GFM','CommonMark'}. A valid lower-case variant like 'gfm' is rejected.

The check `content_type not in value.lower()` uses a substring test on the whole header value. A defaulted `text/plain` can pass if the substring appears in a parameter value, and valid values can be rejected when the type appears only in parameters.
`lhs, op, rhs = result` assumes a 3-element tuple. A malformed marker tuple of different length will raise ValueError.
Replacing only `\n` leaves a stray `\r` from CRLF line endings, producing malformed folded headers.

Interpreter is built from python_version[:2]. For a major-only python_version the slice is a one-element tuple, so _version_nodot receives an invalid input and the resulting interpreter string is wrong / causes a TypeError.
The older-version loop accesses python_version[1] unconditionally. With a major-only version this raises IndexError, contrary to the docstring which says major-only versions are supported.
Scheme check uses `urlsplit(...).scheme != "file"` which is case-sensitive. Upper-case schemes like FILE:// are rejected even though they are valid file URLs.
date_expr and time_expr are still attached to expression when reused in new Add, giving nodes two parents and corrupting the original AST.
end and start are raw SQL strings but self.func expects expressions, causing crash or wrong quoting.
EXTRACT(days FROM interval) returns only the day component, not total days, so WEEK is wrong when difference spans months/years.
Direct dict lookup crashes with KeyError if single-column PRIMARY KEY references a column with no ColumnDef.
Moves table-level PRIMARY KEY to column without checking if column already has a primary-key constraint, creating duplicate PKs.
Presence of vcs_info/archive_info/dir_info is tested with bool(), so a present but falsy object would be counted as absent. The contract requires exactly one is not None.
PyPy ABI tag is specified as pypy38_pp73 with underscores, but code builds 'pypy38-pp73' using '-' join.
GraalPy ABI tag is specified as graalpy_38_native with underscores, but code builds 'graalpy-38-native' using '-' join.
interpreter is built from python_version[:2] with _version_nodot. For a major-only version e.g. (3,) this produces a malformed interpreter and later logic assumes a minor component exists.
The older-version loop accesses python_version[1]. With a major-only python_version this raises IndexError.
platforms = list(platforms or platform_tags()) treats an explicitly passed empty iterable as falsy and substitutes platform_tags(), breaking the documented ability to pass an empty list.
EXTRACT(days FROM interval) returns only the days component, not total days, so differences over a month are wrong. Postgres field should be epoch-based or total days.
Postgres EXTRACT uses singular field DAY, plural days is not recognized and causes a syntax error.
EXTRACT(month)/3 with CAST to BIGINT truncates toward zero, so negative quarter differences are off by one versus floor division.
Advances even when table parsing failed (this is None), skipping a token and allowing malformed ALTER TABLE with missing table to parse with null this.
Requires end-of-input to return Alter, so a trailing semicolon or valid terminator falls through to Command instead of Alter.

_parse_derived_table_values parses a table alias with _parse_table_alias at line 115 and then re-parses an alias again in the Values constructor at line 121 via `alias or self._parse_table_alias()`. The second parse will consume the next token even when alias is None, corrupting the parse stream and potentially raising errors.

After parsing the table name for ALTER, the code unconditionally advances the parser with `if self._next: self._advance()`. This skips the first token after the table unconditionally, losing it and causing the subsequent action parser to start on the wrong token.

The ALTER node is only returned when `if not self._curr` is true. If any token remains after parsing actions/options/cascade, the method falls through to `_parse_as_command(start)`, discarding a correctly parsed ALTER and treating it as a command.

RETURNING is parsed once at line 66 before the source and again at line 97 as `returning or self._parse_returning()`. The second call will attempt to parse RETURNING again if the first call returned falsy, consuming tokens that belong to later clauses and producing wrong results.

The Insert `source` is built with `self._match(TokenType.TABLE) and self._parse_table()`. TokenType.TABLE was already consumed at line 29 for the INSERT ... TABLE syntax, so this second match can incorrectly consume a TABLE keyword that belongs to the following expression or skip parsing entirely.
Uses `if literal:` so a valid 0 index (falsy) in a union like [1,0] is silently dropped instead of appended.
Type dispatch checks `literal` (last parsed element) instead of `indexes[0]`; when len==1 after dropped falsy elements it can pick the wrong node type.
SET parsing runs unconditionally, so INSERT OVERWRITE DIRECTORY ... can be mis-parsed as INSERT ... SET and wrap the Directory in a Schema.
REPLACE token is consumed even when neither WHERE nor USING follows, silently dropping it.
Using `match and parse()` yields False when absent, storing False instead of None for partition/settings.
Using `match and parse()` yields False when TABLE absent, storing False instead of None for source.
Alias is parsed inside parens then again outside with `or`, so an inner alias hides/discards the outer alias and alias is searched in wrong position.
Resolved ClickHouse suffix parts[1] only selects the class but is never stored on the instance, losing the combinator.
When expr is a Window, params are parsed after the window spec and window fix-up ignores params, so param+window order is wrong and window is not re-parsed after params.
After USING ANALYZER with missing name it calls raise_error but continues to build Match with falsy analyzer.
Uses expression.args["alias"] directly, raising KeyError when LATERAL VIEW has no alias, and then dereferences alias.name.
Appends Unnest.offset to the alias columns but never clears offset from the Unnest, and `this` was already rendered on line 3, so ordinality is duplicated/misrendered.
Direct dict lookup defs[...] raises KeyError if single-column PRIMARY KEY references a missing/non-ColumnDef name.
Unconditionally appends PrimaryKeyColumnConstraint even if column already has one, producing duplicate PRIMARY KEY.
Fallback for unknown unit sets unit to AGE(...) interval then does CAST(interval AS BIGINT) which Postgres cannot cast.

env_python_full_version accesses environment["python_full_version"] when environment is a non-empty dict that lacks the key, raising KeyError. The same pattern exists in the earlier select implementation.

Environment marker evaluation uses environment or {} so when environment is None the marker is evaluated against an empty dict instead of default_environment(). The env built for package markers also uses environment or {}.

parse_wheel_filename(wheel.filename)[-1] passes only the platform tag to compatible_tags_selector; the selector needs the full wheel compatibility tags, so wheel selection is incorrect. Same misuse exists in the first select version.
header_store_parse folds newlines with " " * (len(name)+2) spaces, producing over-indented continuation lines and a non-standard header value.

compatible_tags_selector is created with tags if tags is not None else sys_tags(). An explicitly passed empty sequence is now treated as a real tag set, disabling wheel matching and forcing sdist fallback, changing semantics from the prior tags or sys_tags() behavior.
prefer_sdist_predicate is documented to receive NormalizedName but is called with package.name which may be un-normalized, risking predicate mismatches.

tokenizer.check is called with a peek=True argument on lines 11 and 25. The check API does not accept a peek flag, so the call will raise a TypeError / be ignored and the look-ahead is not performed correctly.

When VERSION_PREFIX_TRAIL is present the default message is '.* suffix can only be used with `==` or `!=` operators'. The code then overwrites the message to the pre-release warning when the specifier starts with '!=' or '==' not '==='. This inverts the intent: the pre-release warning is raised for the operators that are allowed and the operator-restriction message is never used for disallowed operators.
For a VERSION_PREFIX_TRAIL error the span_end is set to tokenizer.position + 1. The +1 makes the error span extend past the actual token, producing an incorrect highlight/location.
For VERSION_LOCAL_LABEL_TRAIL the span_end is set to tokenizer.position. The span does not include the local-label trail token, so the reported range is too short.

license_refs is built from the pre-lowercased expression and stores 'LicenseRef-' + ref[len(licenseref_prefix):] preserving the original case of the suffix. Later look-ups use the lowercased final_token, so the canonical form can retain mixed case in the suffix and can KeyError when the original case differs from the lowercased lookup key.
Sample is assigned to pre_alias/post_alias without a leading space, so it is concatenated directly onto the preceding token, e.g. ')SAMPLE' instead of ') SAMPLE'.
Ordinality is built as ' WITH ORDINALITY{alias}' and then appended at the very end of the return string, so WITH ORDINALITY appears after joins/laterals instead of immediately after the table name.
self.expressions returns a SQL string, but self.wrap expects an exp.Expression node. Wrapping a string can crash or produce incorrect output.
arrow_sql is a string returned by arrow_json_extract_sql, but self.wrap expects an expression node, so wrapping the string is a type misuse.
expression.text('unit') can be None; calling .upper() on None raises AttributeError before the 'or DAY' fallback can apply.
For an unrecognised unit the code sets unit = age and returns CAST(AGE(...) AS BIGINT). Casting an interval to BIGINT is invalid PostgreSQL SQL.
PyPy ABI is built with '-' join, e.g. 'pypy38-pp73', but the documented tag is 'pypy38_pp73'. With the current code the ABI is wrong unless _normalize_string later rewrites hyphens.
GraalPy ABI is built with '-' join, e.g. 'graalpy-38-native', but the documented tag is 'graalpy_38_native'. This yields a wrong ABI tag.

raise self._invalid_metadata(msg, cause=defect) from defect uses an email.errors.Defect as the cause. Defect is not a BaseException, so `from defect` raises TypeError and the original validation error is lost.
Charset is compared with `charset != "UTF-8"`. Parameter values are case-insensitive, so 'utf-8' is incorrectly rejected.
Markdown variant is taken from parameters with default 'GFM' and checked against {'GFM','CommonMark'} case-sensitively. A value like 'gfm' is incorrectly rejected.
Assertion rejects MarkerAtom. The type hint allows MarkerAtom but isinstance check only allows list/tuple/str, causing AssertionError for valid input.
The else branch returns `marker` unchanged. For a MarkerAtom input this returns a non-str object, violating the declared return type str and breaking callers.
cpython ABI builds "cp" + soabi.split("-")[1] without checking length. A malformed soabi with no '-' would raise IndexError.
Appending target.this strips table qualifier and column metadata from Schema; qualified SET assignments lose information.
REPLACE is consumed even when not followed by WHERE/USING, silently dropping the token and mis-parsing the statement.
EXTRACT(month FROM age)/3 uses float division then CAST truncation toward zero, wrong for negative intervals; needs floor/integer division.
Unsupported units fall through to CAST(AGE(...) AS BIGINT) which is invalid Postgres SQL.
Calls _parse_table_alias() twice; second call re-parses from same position and can consume a following clause as alias.
INDEXED BY is emitted after alias, but SQLite syntax requires table INDEXED BY before alias.
WITH ORDINALITY is appended at end of table_sql after joins/laterals/pivots instead of immediately after table/alias.
FETCH FIRST ROW ONLY can omit count, but conversion builds Limit with expression=None instead of 1, generating invalid/wrong LIMIT.
SESSION branch never advances to the action token and the else branch checks _next instead of _curr, so parser lookup uses the wrong _prev token.
Guard `if literal:` drops valid falsy bracket elements like index 0 or empty-string key in a union, losing elements.
Test `isinstance(literal,str) or literal is not False` accepts None as valid, creating a subscript/union with None instead of raising ParseError.
Single key/slice is wrapped in JSONPathKey/Subscript/Selector but union leaves raw str/int parts unwrapped, breaking the AST contract.
The combinator suffix in parts[1] is never stored on the new node; instance is built only with this/expressions so e.g. sumIf loses If.
First parens (params) were parsed as anon_func.expressions and second parens as params, but code keeps first as expressions and second as params, swapping args and params.
Parser.expression expects a class, not an instance; passing instance causes TypeError.
Invalid paths starting with lax/strict never warn even under STRICT_JSON_PATH_SYNTAX, silently hiding syntax errors.
Parser.expression expects a class; passing an exp.Match instance crashes.
Parser.expression expects a class; passing an exp.Not instance crashes.
_match is called with expression=properties[-1] which is not a valid parameter. The call raises TypeError and the comma is never correctly consumed.
If a property is parsed but the following comma is missing, _match does not advance, so the next loop iteration re-parses the same token leading to an infinite loop / duplicate parse.
Unconditional self._advance() after parsing the table discards the next token, misaligning the parser for the ALTER action keyword.
Parser is looked up from self._prev.text.upper() after the table has been parsed and after the spurious advance, so _prev no longer points to the action keyword.

The while condition calls self._match(TokenType.COMMA) as a side effect and then checks self._prev.token_type, which consumes the comma before the loop body runs and makes the parser lookup unreliable.
The ALTER node is only returned when not self._curr, i.e. at EOF. Any valid ALTER with trailing whitespace or a following statement is incorrectly fallen back to _parse_as_command.
Factor is concatenated directly to the EXTRACT expression without an operator or spacing, producing invalid SQL like EXTRACT(epoch FROM ...) *123.
EXTRACT(days FROM interval) returns the days component of the interval, not the total number of days, so the WEEK calculation is incorrect for intervals spanning months/years.
For units without a factor and not WEEK/MONTH/QUARTER/YEAR, unit is set to the AGE interval and then CAST(... AS BIGINT) is emitted, which is invalid PostgreSQL and yields wrong results.

Wheel filenames are split from the left with `filename.split('-', dashes-2)`. The distribution name part can legally contain hyphens after normalization, so splitting from the left can consume hyphens that belong to the name and assign the wrong value to name/version/build/tag. Splitting must be performed from the right.
_wheel_name_regex.match(name_part) only matches at the start of the string. A name that has a valid prefix followed by illegal characters would be accepted. The check should require a full match.

env_python_full_version is obtained with `environment['python_full_version'] if environment else ...`. If the caller passes a non-empty dict that does not contain `python_full_version`, a KeyError is raised. The code should fall back to the default environment for missing keys.

Environment markers are evaluated with `environment or {}`. When `environment` is None the spec requires `default_environment()` to be used, just like for `python_full_version`. Evaluating with an empty dict can cause markers to be incorrectly unsatisfied.

Build tag parsing creates `(int(build_match.group(1)), build_match.group(2))`. If the regex makes group 2 optional, `group(2)` can be None, producing a BuildTag containing None where a string is expected and breaking downstream code.

`_parse_local_version(match.group('local'))` is called unconditionally. When the version has no local segment the regex group is None, which can cause `_parse_local_version` to crash if it expects a string.
Direct dict lookup crashes with KeyError if the single-column primary key references a missing/ differently-quoted column or a non-column expression.
Adds a duplicate PrimaryKeyColumnConstraint even if the column already has one, producing two PRIMARY KEYs.
Multi-path handling only triggers for JSONExtract, so multi-path JSONExtractScalar falls through to single-path arrow logic and drops paths.
Truthiness test drops valid falsy indexes like 0, so [0,1] or [0,0] loses elements.
Union keeps raw str/int/slice values instead of wrapping them as JSONPathKey/JSONPathSubscript like the single-element path does.
A slice or other JSONPathPart that is not Script/Filter is wrapped in JSONPathSubscript instead of being returned directly.

milli.pop() and nano.pop() mutate expression.args and remove the values. After the pop the lists can become empty, so the later `if milli or nano` test is false and the updated sec is never written back, and the original args are destroyed.
sec is an Expression node, not a numeric value. Using `sec += ...` relies on Python in-place arithmetic on an Expression which does not build a proper SQL expression tree.
zone.pop() mutates expression.args and assumes zone is a mutable list. If zone is a single node pop will raise, and the mutation is a side effect on the original tree.
column = defs[primary_key.expressions[0].name] assumes the primary key column is present in defs. If the column is missing a KeyError is raised.
The check `self._curr.token_type == TokenType.VAR` prevents matching MATCH operators that are represented as keywords rather than VAR tokens, so valid MATCH syntax is missed.
lax/strict prefix check is case-sensitive, so valid uppercase LAX/STRICT paths still trigger a warning and are treated as invalid.
Requiring TokenType.VAR misses MATCH tokenized as its own type, so plain `x MATCH y` is not parsed and MATCH becomes an alias.
Converting Fetch to Limit copies only count, dropping PERCENT and WITH TIES, so e.g. FETCH WITH TIES becomes LIMIT with different results.
Using sep="" concatenates query modifiers without spaces, producing invalid SQL like `...WHERE...ORDER...`.

The Combined/Parameterized agg instance is built with this=anon_func.this which is the full ClickHouse name e.g. 'countDistinct'. The base name parts[0] returned by _resolve_clickhouse_agg is never used and the suffix parts[1] is never stored, so the resulting AST keeps the wrong function name and loses the suffix information.

Condition `isinstance(literal, str) or literal is not False` is too permissive. It accepts None and any non-False object, so a None literal can be added to indexes and later used as this for JSONPathSubscript, leading to invalid nodes/crashes.

After a comma the loop parses the next slice and only appends it when the permissive test passes. If the slice is empty/false the value is silently skipped, so '[a,,b]' or '[a,]' is accepted without raising 'Cannot have empty segment'.

ParseError/TokenError from parse_json_path is caught and a warning is logged only when STRICT_JSON_PATH_SYNTAX is true and the text does not start with lax/strict. In all other cases the error is swallowed and the original literal is returned, silently hiding invalid JSON path syntax.
milli is taken from expression.args and .pop() is called on it. The arg is mutated and pop assumes a list; if it is a single node AttributeError is raised and the expression is mutated for callers.
nano.pop() mutates expression.args and assumes nano is a list. Same side-effect / AttributeError risk as milli.

sec is an expression node from expression.args.get('sec'). Using sec += ... attempts in-place addition of an expression node with a numeric literal, which is not a valid node operation and will produce wrong SQL or raise TypeError.
zone is obtained from args and zone.pop() is used. This mutates the expression and assumes zone is a list; if it is a single node it crashes.
self.sql(expression, 'this') is called with a second positional argument. The generator sql method does not accept a key this way, so the rendered SQL is incorrect or raises.

end and start are plain SQL strings built on lines 45-46, but they are passed to self.func('DATE_TRUNC', ...). func expects expression nodes; a string is rendered as a literal, producing SQL like DATE_TRUNC('UNIT','CAST(...)') instead of DATE_TRUNC('UNIT', CAST(...)).
The factor is concatenated directly into the SQL string: EXTRACT(...){factor}. If DATE_DIFF_FACTOR does not include a leading operator/space, the generated SQL is syntactically invalid.
column = defs[primary_key.expressions[0].name] will raise KeyError if the primary-key column definition is not present in defs, e.g. column defined later or with different casing.
column.constraints may be None for a column without constraints. Enumerating None raises TypeError.

auto_increment is removed from column.constraints and then inserted at primary_key_index. After removal the list shrinks, so primary_key_index is off by one and the auto_increment ends up in the wrong position.
Uses expression.args["alias"] and alias.name without guard; view Lateral with no alias raises KeyError / AttributeError.
Dereferences expression.this.args without checking for None; Lateral with no this crashes.
Copies only this and expressions, dropping other Anonymous args like distinct.
Passes an instance to self.expression() which expects an expression class, causing TypeError.
Calls milli.pop() mutating the parsed expression and fails if milli is a single expression or empty list.
Same pop/mutation bug for nano as for milli.
Tests `if milli or nano` after popping, so single-element lists are now empty and sec update is never set.
The view branch assumes an alias is present and accesses expression.args["alias"] directly and then alias.name. If the Lateral node has view=True but no alias, a KeyError / AttributeError is raised.

When ordinality is present the alias string " AS …" is moved into the ordinality fragment and alias is cleared. The resulting SQL becomes "WITH ORDINALITY AS alias" which is dialect dependent and loses the original placement of the alias; with an empty alias it produces a trailing "WITH ORDINALITY" with no alias handling.

LIMIT/FETCH conversion creates a new exp.Limit/exp.Fetch object in the local variable limit but never writes it back to expression.args["limit"]. Later helpers that read expression.args["limit"] see the stale node type, causing inconsistent rendering.

Inside the comma loop a parsed slice is appended only if `if literal:` is true. Falsy but valid values such as 0 or an empty string are silently dropped, producing a missing index and a wrong JSONPathUnion / incorrect parse state.

For a single-element bracket the node type is decided from the last parsed `literal` variable rather than from `indexes[0]`. If a comma was consumed and a later slice was falsy and skipped, the type check uses the wrong value, leading to JSONPathKey/Selector/Subscript mis-classification.

The guard `isinstance(literal, str) or literal is not False` lets None and other non-false values pass. Subsequent node creation can receive `this=None`, which downstream renderers do not expect and may crash.

_parse_derived_table_values parses an alias into `alias` and then builds Values with `alias or self._parse_table_alias()`. When `alias` is None a second call to `_parse_table_alias()` is made, consuming tokens that belong to the following clause and potentially producing a wrong alias or losing input.
For a derived VALUES form the closing parenthesis is matched after the alias is parsed. The alias therefore is attempted inside the parentheses, which is the wrong order for `VALUES (...) [alias]`.

`alternative = self._match_texts(self.INSERT_ALTERNATIVES) and self._prev.text` yields False when OR is present but no alternative matches, instead of keeping alternative as None. Downstream code expects None or a string.

Returning is parsed early at line 66 for T-SQL and then parsed again with `returning or self._parse_returning()` at line 97. The second parse can consume tokens already examined or cause the clause to be parsed twice.

Kind is derived with `self._curr.text.upper().partition('_')[2] or None`. For operators without an underscore, e.g. REGEXP, partition returns an empty string and kind becomes None, losing the operator information.
Checks _next instead of _curr, so a final single-token action is never consumed and ALTER falls back to Command.
Direct dict indexing with _prev.text crashes with KeyError and is wrong for multi-word ALTER_PARSERS keys matched by _match_texts.
EXTRACT(days FROM interval) returns only day component, so WEEK is wrong for intervals spanning months/years.
Fallback sets unit to AGE interval then CASTs interval AS BIGINT which is invalid Postgres.
When no alternative matches, expression is False instead of None due to `and` short-circuit.
Missing closing paren in derived (VALUES ...) is silently accepted via optional _match_r_paren.
When expression.args.get('view') is truthy the code accesses expression.args['alias'] directly. If alias is missing a KeyError is raised.
expression.this is dereferenced without a None check, so expression.this.args.get('offset') raises AttributeError for a Lateral without a this.
table_alias comes from expression.args.get('alias') and may be None, yet self.sql(table_alias) is called unconditionally.
defs[primary_key.expressions[0].name] assumes the primary-key column definition is present in defs; a missing column raises KeyError.
For units not handled explicitly the code sets unit = age and returns CAST(unit AS BIGINT). AGE returns an interval and casting an interval to BIGINT is invalid in Postgres.
Quarter difference is computed as EXTRACT(year)*4 + EXTRACT(month)/3, which yields fractional values and does not correctly count quarters.
After parsing the table, WITH CHECK and ON property the code unconditionally advances when a next token exists, discarding a token that should be processed by the ALTER parser.
The Alter node is only returned when self._curr is falsy; otherwise the function falls through to _parse_as_command, causing valid ALTER statements with remaining input to be mis-parsed as a command.
The generated SQL concatenates the epoch extract with factor without an operator, e.g. `... )86400`, producing invalid PostgreSQL.
When unit is not matched the code falls back to `unit = age` and then does `CAST({unit} AS BIGINT)`, which tries to cast PostgreSQL AGE to BIGINT and is invalid.
Alias is parsed at line 233 and then line 239 does `alias or self._parse_table_alias()`, reparsing the alias when the first parse returned None and consuming an extra token.

The LIMIT/FETCH conversion creates a new limit node in a local variable but never writes it back to expression.args['limit']. Downstream code that inspects the expression still sees the original node, leading to inconsistent generation.

Advancing only when self._next exists makes the parser off-by-one when the action keyword is the last token. In that case self._prev stays on the table token and parser = ALTER_PARSERS.get(self._prev.text.upper()) is wrong.

The while condition uses self._match(TokenType.COMMA) which consumes a comma as a side effect. The condition also mixes a consuming match with a non-consuming check, corrupting parser state and potentially skipping or looping forever.

Limit subtracts 1 for closing paren but does not reserve space for trailing comma when include_trailing_comma is true, allowing over-length lines.

File-level skip raises even when raise_on_skip=False, so streaming call with raise_on_skip=False still raises.
Atomic mode needs a seekable/readable buffer but tests readable(); a seekable check is required for later seek(0)/read().

When preserve_trailing_comma is true a fitting single-line literal is forced to multiline instead of staying single-line.

set() on a single string path splits it into characters, corrupting src_paths when a string is supplied.
value_end sums lines[:end_lineno] including the end line itself then adds end_col_offset, overshooting and dropping trailing content like comments.

Returns early when comments are present and falls through to iterate when comments is empty/None, opposite of docstring.

Increments `max_ticks += 0` so opening tick count stays 0 and no code span is ever matched.
Replaces double backslash `'\\\\'` instead of single backslash, so backslash-escaped text is not stashed.

Generates IDs starting at `toc_0` due to no-op `index + 0`; should be 1-based.

Break condition is inverted: it breaks when a definition marker is found instead of when it is absent, so no definitions are ever collected.
Loose state is overwritten instead of accumulated, so a prior loose definition is lost when a later tight definition is seen.
start skips two characters instead of the single '<', dropping the first character of the href and mis-parsing short autolinks.

The loop pops the next import with interface['imports'].pop(1) instead of pop(0). This skips elements, changes ordering and eventually raises IndexError when only one import remains.
After append the new index should be len(notes)-1, but len(notes)-2 gives -1 for first footnote and duplicates/shifts all indexes.
Only lower() is applied; leading whitespace/control characters like '   javascript:' bypass startswith check but browsers still execute it as harmful protocol.
tuple(string) splits a single string protocol into single characters, so startswith matches almost any URL and allows harmful protocols.
If directive has no title relpath is None, os.path.join/isabs/realpath crashes instead of returning block_error.
os.path.commonpath raises ValueError on different drives/mixed absolute-relative paths, crashing render instead of returning block_error.
Uses - instead of + for string concatenation, raising TypeError on any circular include instead of returning block_error.
User-controlled encoding can be unknown raising LookupError, and decode can raise UnicodeDecodeError, crashing instead of block_error.
Extension check is case-sensitive, so .MD/.HTML files are not recognized and fall through to wrong token type.
Exposes absolute server filesystem path dest in attrs['filepath'] to rendered output.
The test `"/" in file_names` checks for the literal list element '/' instead of detecting a path that contains '/'. The root-directory safeguard therefore never triggers for paths like '/etc'.
