`value_end` is computed with `lines[: end_lineno - 0]` which sums the whole end line and then adds `end_col_offset`. The offset is therefore too large and trailing comments / whitespace after the literal are lost or duplicated.

Conditional expression precedence makes `arguments.get("filename", None) or os.getcwd() if file_names == ["-"] else ...` parse as `arguments.get(...) or (os.getcwd() if ... else ...)`. Filename therefore overrides the streaming branch incorrectly.
In atomic mode `_internal_output` can be the original output_stream which is readable but not seekable, e.g. stdout. Calling `_internal_output.seek(0)` then raises.
When FileSkipped is caught, `input_stream.read()` is executed after `api.sort_stream` has already consumed the stream, so the fallback write outputs empty data.
`sort_stream` raises `FileSkipSetting` at line 54, but `main` catches `FileSkipped`. The skip exception is therefore not handled and propagates.
The 'ies' -> 'y' rule fires for any preceding consonant, so words whose plural is just 'ie' + 's' are mis-singularized, e.g. 'pies' -> 'py', 'movies' -> 'movy'.
The 'es' rule only strips 'es' when preceded by 's' (pattern 'ses'). Plurals like 'boxes', 'watches', 'dishes' fall through to the generic -s strip and become 'boxe', 'watche', etc.

The loop `for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES` expects each element to be a pair of pairs. With a normal size/symbol list it raises ValueError, and with an empty ranges list `size` is never defined leading to NameError on hnbytes computation.
If abs_bytes is >= the largest next_size the loop ends without break, leaving size at the second-last tier and under-reporting very large values.
`if others: return` causes update to return immediately whenever arguments are supplied, so no elements are ever added and the following elif/else branches are unreachable.
Condition is inverted: returns 'Could not find file' when file exists and tries to open when it does not exist, causing wrong results and FileNotFoundError.
URL is lowercased but not stripped/normalized, so leading spaces or control chars like '  javascript:...' bypass startswith check.
open/decode can raise OSError, LookupError for bad encoding, or UnicodeDecodeError, crashing instead of returning block_error.
Stores absolute real filesystem path dest in output attrs, leaking server layout.
Any backslash causes failure, so escaped '<', '>' or other chars inside <...> link destination are rejected though CommonMark allows escaped chars.
Loop only breaks on DD_START_RE and consumes any other line as a definition, so non-definition blocks after definitions are swallowed.
Loose is appended before updating and overwritten instead of accumulated, so a blank line in current text marks only the next item and prior looseness is lost.
p.replace("3", _repl_w, 1) replaces the first literal '3' anywhere in the pattern, corrupting patterns containing '3' elsewhere.
(?<=\n) never matches at start of string, so a list-break rule at position 0 is missed.
The guard returns "" when imports are present, so the function never processes any imports and always returns empty for the intended case.
Condition `if not file_names or not show_config` prints the quick guide and returns early even when `show_config` is True without files, preventing config display.
`"/" in file_names` tests list membership, not whether any path contains a slash, so the recursive-root failsafe is ineffective.
The slice `lines[: 1 - end_lineno]` is inverted; it does not sum the lines before the end line, causing wrong `value_end` and duplicated / lost trailing comment.
On `FileSkipped` the code does `output_stream.write(input_stream.read())` after `sort_stream` has already consumed the input stream, so nothing is written.
loose state is overwritten instead of accumulated, so a previous loose definition is lost when current text has no blank line.
Backslash is rejected outright instead of treated as escape, so valid <...> destinations with escaped characters fail to parse.
If parse_title returns None/empty, os.path.join and realpath will crash or misbehave instead of returning a block_error.
os.path.commonpath raises ValueError on different drives or mixed absolute/relative paths, crashing instead of returning block_error.
Uses `-` instead of `+` for string concatenation, raising TypeError when circular reference is detected.
decode(encoding) can raise LookupError for unknown encoding and UnicodeDecodeError for invalid bytes, crashing the parse.
After appending a new key, len(notes)-2 is one too low, so the first footnote gets index 0 instead of 1.
Default heading_id uses index + 0 so ids start at toc_0 instead of toc_1.
replace() rewrites the first " {0,3}" anywhere, corrupting rules with no indent prefix like a "{3,}" marker run.
import_start - from_import tries to subtract two strings, causing a TypeError at runtime in the force_single_line path.

The loop uses `if index <= lines_after_imports` and then accesses blank_lines[index]. When index == lines_after_imports the access is out of range, and with lines_after_imports == 0 it is out of range on the first iteration.
Insertion uses formatted_output[output_at:0] = output. The slice does not reliably insert at output_at and is semantically wrong.
Blank lines after imports are inserted with formatted_output[imports_tail:0] = blank_lines, which is an incorrect slice for insertion at imports_tail.

in_quote returned by _parse_utils.skip_line is not persisted across iterations; it is re-initialised to "" each loop, so multi-line quoted strings are not tracked and next_construct detection is wrong.
When a nested comment is processed, use_comments is set to [] if from_imports remain, discarding accumulated comments that should be attached to the current import line.
Existence of a section heading comment is tested only against parsed.lines_without_imports[0:1]; duplicate headings can be inserted if the comment is not on the very first line.
Existence of a section footer comment is tested only against parsed.lines_without_imports[-1:], so a footer can be duplicated if it is not on the very last line.
Looseness is overwritten instead of accumulated; once a blank line makes a list loose it must stay loose.
Returns empty href for "<>"; an autolink/angle href must be non-empty.
Only rejects < \ \n \r \x00, so spaces, tabs and other ASCII controls are accepted as valid autolink href.
Condition is inverted: existing files report "Could not find file" and missing files fall through to open() and crash.
open/read/decode can raise OSError, LookupError for bad encoding, and UnicodeDecodeError, crashing the parse instead of returning block_error.
os.path.commonpath raises ValueError on different drives/empty paths, crashing the build.
relpath from parse_title can be None/empty; os.path.join/realpath/commonpath then raise TypeError/ValueError.
Condition is inverted: existing list is discarded to [] and None stays None, causing loss of prior footnotes and crash on enumerate/contains of None.
Skips two chars instead of '<', truncating first character of href.
Breaks when line is a definition start, so no definitions are collected; should break when not a definition.
Overwrites loose flag instead of latching, so a blank line in an earlier definition is forgotten for later ones.

Uses `if not notes` / `if not indexes` instead of `is None`, so a valid empty list/dict is discarded and rebuilt. This loses aliasing and desynchronizes `footnotes` from `footnote_indexes`, producing duplicate indexes.
Default `heading_id` does `index-1` while caller passes 0-based `i`, so first heading gets `toc_-1` and all ids are shifted.

Uniqueness via `_unique_id` is only applied when `auto_heading_id` is true, so a custom `heading_id` that collides with existing ids or repeats produces duplicate `id` attributes and broken TOC links.
`.replace(...,1)` rewrites only the first `{0,3}` indent quantifier, leaving later indent bounds at 3 and making break detection too permissive/strict for nested rules.
Lookbehind `(?<=\n)` never matches at position 0 so a break at start of string is missed, and if `pairs` is empty the compiled pattern `""` matches everywhere causing wrong splits/loops.
‘/’ in file_names tests list membership of the literal string ‘/’ instead of checking if any filename contains a slash, so the recursive-root failsafe never triggers.
On FileSkipped the code reads input_stream again. The stream has already been consumed by api.sort_stream, so the write is empty / partial and the original input is lost.
Inline comments are extended from parsed.categorized_comments['straight'][module] but the entry is never removed. The comments remain in parsed and can be emitted again on a later pass.
Direct indexing parsed.imports[section][...][module] assumes the module key exists; a missing key raises KeyError.
After popping flags, arguments still contains config keys, so ‘if arguments:’ is always true and the CLI exits with ‘arguments passed in without any paths’ even for valid config options.
next_import is split on spaces and re-joined, destroying import syntax with aliases, ‘as’, or multiple tokens and producing incorrect wrapped output.
When inline_comments are present but all falsy, line_content is built as ‘…  #’ leaving a trailing comment marker with no text.

Operator precedence makes the expression arguments.get('filename',None) or os.getcwd() if file_names == ['-'] else … evaluate as filename overriding the streaming check, yielding a wrong settings_path.
max_ticks is incremented by 0 instead of 1, so the opening backtick count is always zero and code span detection never finds a matching closing span.
ord(start[-1]) is evaluated before checking that start is non-empty, causing IndexError when i is at or past the end of rawdata.
Condition uses `isinstance(el.tag, str) or self.header_rgx.match(el.tag)`. The `or` makes every string tag pass, so non-header elements are processed and later code assumes a header tag.
int(el.tag[-1]) assumes the tag ends with a digit 1-6. With non-header tags processed by the bug above it raises ValueError.
def run is indented under the unique function, making it a nested function instead of a class method. It will never be called as the extension’s run method.
Uses `-` instead of `+` for string concatenation, so reporting a circular include raises TypeError instead of returning a block_error.
Checks _url.startswith without stripping leading whitespace/control characters, so ' javascript:...' or '\njavascript:...' bypasses the harmful-protocol block.
Only auto-generated ids are de-duplicated via _unique_id; custom heading_id values can collide with each other or existing HTML ids producing duplicate id attributes.
Stores absolute resolved filesystem path in attrs["filepath"] which leaks server directory layout into rendered output/env.
When combine_straight_imports is enabled and there are no as imports, the function returns [] for a non-empty straight_modules list, discarding all imports instead of combining them.
The test `"/" in file_names` checks list membership, not whether any path contains '/'. Paths like '/etc' bypass the root recursion guard.
next_statement.split(line_separator)[-2] raises IndexError when next_statement has only one line, causing a crash.
imports.pop(0) mutates the caller's imports list, causing unexpected side effects for the caller.
When inline comments are empty the code builds a line ending with '  #', producing a stray comment marker.
Converting src_paths to set discards ordering and may break Config expectations for a sequence.
On FileSkipped the code does input_stream.read() after sort_stream may have already consumed stdin, resulting in empty output.

The loop pops interface["imports"] with pop(1) instead of pop(0). This skips the first remaining import, processes imports out of order and raises IndexError when only one import is left, resulting in missing imports or a crash.

value_end is computed as sum(len(line) for line in lines[: end_lineno - 0]) + end_col_offset, i.e. sum of the end line itself plus offset. The correct offset needs the sum of lines before end_lineno only. The off-by-one causes the trailing comment after the literal to be dropped or mis-copied.

When sort_stream raises FileSkipped the code does output_stream.write(input_stream.read()). The input_stream has already been consumed by sort_stream, so read() returns empty and the original stdin content is lost.

src_paths is forced to set(config_dict.get("src_paths", ())). Converting to set discards ordering and duplicates, breaking the comment about keeping CLI-provided values as-is for later wildcard expansion.
Default heading_id returns "toc_" + str(index-1), so first heading (i=0) gets "toc_-1". Off-by-one gives wrong/negative ids.
Condition is inverted: existing files return "Could not find file" and missing files fall through to open() and crash with FileNotFoundError.
URL is only lowercased, not stripped. Leading spaces/control chars like "  javascript:..." bypass startswith check and render harmful link.
Storing os.path.realpath dest in attrs["filepath"] leaks absolute server filesystem path into tokens/output.
Error message construction uses '-' between strings: "Could not include circular reference: " - relpath, which is a SyntaxError and prevents import.
The test `if notes: notes = []` resets the existing footnotes list to empty when notes are present, discarding prior notes and corrupting indexes.
When `footnotes` is not set, `notes` is None, so `key not in notes` and `notes.append(key)` raise TypeError.
os.path.commonpath raises ValueError if source_dir and dest are on different drives, causing a crash on Windows.
A second `def toc_hook` is defined after the hook is already appended to `md.before_render_hooks`, shadowing the first definition and never being registered.
lengths_desc[0] raises IndexError when iterables is empty instead of yielding nothing.
Condition e_ < 0 is never true because errors only increase, so secondaries are never yielded and primary raises StopIteration.
Error should be decreased after yielding a secondary, not increased, otherwise scheduling is inverted.
strict=True just yields slices without checking length, so no ValueError is ever raised.

_parse_angle_link_href assumes pos points at '<' and starts the href at pos+2, skipping the first character after '<'. The returned href is therefore missing its first character and the end position is off.

The invalid character set includes '<' and '\\'. The '<' check makes the parser reject a href as soon as a '<' is seen inside the scan window and the backslash rejection is overly aggressive for an angle-bracket href, causing valid inputs to be rejected with None,None.

DD_MARKER_RE.sub("  ", src[start:pos], count=1) replaces the first occurrence of the marker anywhere in the collected definition slice, not necessarily at the start of the line. If the marker pattern appears later in the definition body the wrong text is replaced.

pairs = [(n, p.replace("3", _repl_w, 1)) ...] replaces the first literal '3' character anywhere in the rule pattern. This can corrupt quantifiers, character classes or other literals that happen to contain '3' instead of only changing the leading-width token.

The regex is built with r"(?P<%s>(?<=
)%s)" % pair. The lookbehind (?<=\n) prevents a match at the very start of the document and the % formatting will raise / mis-interpret if a rule pattern itself contains '%' characters.
The file-existence test is inverted: `if os.path.isfile(dest)` returns a “Could not find file” error when the file exists and lets a non-existent file fall through to `open`, causing a crash.
Footnote index is assigned as `len(notes) - 2` after appending, giving -1 for the first note and off-by-one for all others.
Default `heading_id` returns `"toc_" + str(index - 1)`, so the first heading gets id `toc_-1`.
A second `toc_hook` definition is created after the hook is already appended to `md.before_render_hooks`. The second definition shadows the first and is never registered, leaving duplicate dead code.
Footnote index is set to len(notes)-2 after appending the key, so the first note gets index -1 and all subsequent notes are off by one. The token then uses indexes[key]+1, producing wrong numbers.
The circular-include error message is built with the subtraction operator " - relpath" instead of string concatenation, causing a TypeError at runtime whenever a circular reference is detected.

Path containment is checked with os.path.commonpath([source_dir, dest]) != source_dir. commonpath can raise ValueError on Windows different drives and can be bypassed by sibling paths that share a prefix, e.g. source_dir=/tmp/a and dest=/tmp/ab, allowing directory traversal.
count(-1, n) makes the first slice seq[-1:n-1] which is empty, so takewhile stops immediately and sliced always yields nothing.
With no iterables, lengths_desc[0]/iters_desc[0] raises IndexError instead of yielding nothing.
iterables/lengths are indexed and len() is called, so a generator/iterator outer iterable is consumed or not subscriptable.
Condition is inverted: it keeps (k+1)-components already contained in a k-component instead of propagating those not contained.
List subtraction is unsupported in Python and raises TypeError when subgraph has unmatched parts.
Non-string input crashes on `" " in t` because str() conversion only applies when already a string.
Error accumulation sign is inverted: errors only grow so `e_ < 0` never fires and secondaries are never yielded.
Empty `iterables`/`lengths` indexes `lengths_desc[0]` and raises IndexError instead of yielding nothing.
Fast path starts search at `start+1`, skipping a match at `start` and breaking negative `start`.
Strict mode just re-yields slices without checking length, never raising ValueError on remainder.
`n == 0` is allowed but invalid; count(0,0) then raises an unrelated ValueError.
The init is inverted: `if notes: notes = []` discards an existing footnotes list and leaves notes empty when it should only initialise when missing. This loses previously collected footnotes.
With the inverted init, `notes` can stay None. `enumerate(notes)` and later `key not in notes` / `notes.append(key)` then raise TypeError.
Parsing an angle-bracket link starts at `pos + 2` instead of `pos + 1`, so the first character of the href is skipped and the returned href is wrong.
The definition is appended with the previous iteration's `loose` flag and `loose` is updated afterwards, so each definition receives the loose value of the preceding definition, an off-by-one.
range(max_k, 0, -0) uses step 0, which always raises ValueError: range() arg 3 must not be zero.

Isinstance check against OutEdgeDataView does not detect multigraph edge views; undirected MultiGraph edges are OutMultiEdgeDataView/MultiEdgeDataView, so multiedges take the simple-edge path and simple graphs are misclassified.
Only wraps in quotes when string contains a space and never escapes embedded double-quotes or handles other whitespace, producing malformed Pajek output that cannot round-trip.
Fast path starts with i=start then searches from i+1, so index start is never checked and negative start is corrupted.
with suppress(ValueError) encloses yield, so a ValueError thrown into the generator by the consumer is incorrectly suppressed.
Errors only increase so e_ < 0 never fires; secondaries are never yielded and primary raises StopIteration.
indexes[key] is set to len(notes)-2 after appending the key, so the first footnote gets index -1 and all subsequent numbers are off by one.
footnote_ref token is created with raw set to the normalized key instead of the original match text m.group(0), breaking raw reconstruction.

toc_hook is defined a second time with the same body after it has already been appended to md.before_render_hooks. The second definition shadows the first and is never used, indicating a copy-paste error.
Uniqueness via _unique_id is only applied when auto_heading_id is True. With a user supplied heading_id duplicates against existing HTML ids are not prevented.
If _get_list_break_rules returns an empty list, regex becomes the empty string and re.compile('') matches everywhere, which can cause runaway matching.

The allow-all branch uses `is True` identity and the later check does `tuple(self._allow_harmful_protocols)`. For a truthy non-bool/non-iterable value e.g. 1 the first branch is skipped and `tuple(1)` raises TypeError, and for a truthy iterable the identity test is brittle. This can crash or bypass the intended allow-list logic.
start = pos + 2 assumes pos points to '<' and skips two characters, so the first character of the URL inside angle brackets is dropped.
The while loop advances with `pos += len(line)`. If `_get_line` returns an empty string or `_scan_definition_tail` does not move `pos`, `pos` stays unchanged and the loop never terminates.

DD_MARKER_RE.sub("  ", src[start:pos], count=1) replaces the definition marker with two spaces instead of removing the marker indentation and ':' as the comment describes, corrupting the extracted definition text.

toc_hook is defined a second time after it was already appended to md.before_render_hooks. The second definition shadows the first and is never registered, leaving duplicate dead code and indicating a copy-paste error.
Error message is built with '-' instead of '+': "Could not include circular reference: " - relpath. This raises TypeError at runtime and crashes include handling.

On circular reference or missing file errors source_file is popped early from include_stack, then the finally block pops again, corrupting/underflowing the stack and potentially popping unrelated entries.
list_item concatenates raw text into <li> without escaping, allowing HTML injection/XSS if text contains markup.
sum(kappas) sums dict keys, not hidden-degree values, so mean_degree is wrong when kappas is given.
Angular distance is negated: |pi-diff|-pi is in [-pi,0] instead of [0,pi], so R*angle is negative and math.pow with non-integer beta raises ValueError.
list minus list is unsupported in Python, so unmatched subgraph partitions crash instead of being appended.
Condition is inverted: non-empty graph returns immediately with no yields, so largest_common_subgraph never computes anything.

File existence test is inverted: `if os.path.isfile(dest)` returns a block_error "Could not find file" when the file does exist, and allows execution to continue when it does not. This yields wrong results for existing includes and causes a crash when opening a missing file.
os.path.commonpath raises ValueError when source_dir and dest are on different drives on Windows. The check can therefore crash instead of safely rejecting an out-of-tree include.
A backslash character is treated as an immediate terminator for an angle-bracket href, returning None, None. This rejects valid escaped sequences inside a URL and changes parsing results.

The loose flag is updated after appending the current definition, so the tuple stored for the current item uses the previous iteration's loose value. This off-by-one propagates an incorrect loose flag to the next definition.
Auto heading_id is defined as 'toc_' + str(index - 1). For the first heading i=0 the id becomes 'toc_-1', producing a negative/duplicate id and breaking the toc contract.

toc_hook is defined a second time after it has already been appended to md.before_render_hooks. The second definition shadows the name and is never used, leaving dead duplicate code and making maintenance error-prone.
if not notes: notes = [] treats an existing empty list as missing, recreates a new list and loses the original env reference. This can cause footnotes to be lost or duplicated across calls.
footnote_ref token is emitted with raw set to key instead of the original matched text m.group(0). The rendered output will lose the original markup.
tok["attrs"]["level"] is accessed without verifying that attrs exists. A heading token without attrs will raise KeyError during TOC generation.
Subtracting lists with `-` raises TypeError and also has wrong logic; unmatched subgraph parts should be appended to new_sg_p.
Angular distance is negated (`fabs(...)-pi` instead of `pi-fabs(...)`), yielding a non-positive angle so `R*angle` is negative and `math.pow` fails or gives wrong p_ij.
Condition is inverted: non-strings are never converted to str, so iterating `t` crashes for e.g. int and non-strings are returned unchanged instead of string representation.
_parse_angle_link_href sets start = pos + 2, skipping the first character after '<'. The returned href is therefore truncated / wrong.
Circular include error builds the message with '-' between two strings: "Could not include circular reference: " - relpath, which raises TypeError at runtime.
os.path.commonpath([source_dir, dest]) raises ValueError on Windows when the two paths are on different drives, causing an unhandled crash in the include safety check.
The loose flag is appended with the previous iteration's value and only then updated from the current text, so each definition is paired with the loose state of the preceding definition.

A second toc_hook function is defined with the same name but never appended to md.before_render_hooks. The first definition is the one actually used, so the duplicate is dead code and shadows the intended hook.
Auto heading id is built as 'toc_' + str(index - 1). With enumerate starting at 0 the first id becomes 'toc_-1'.
The existence test is inverted: if os.path.isfile(dest) returns error 'Could not find file'. Valid files are rejected and missing files fall through to open.
Because of the inverted isfile check, a non-existent dest is not rejected and open(dest,'rb') raises FileNotFoundError unhandled.

finally unconditionally pops include_stack for dest and optionally for source_file. If an early return/pop has already altered the stack, the pops can remove the wrong entry or raise IndexError, corrupting include detection.

safe_url uses 'if self._allow_harmful_protocols is True' identity check and then tuple(self._allow_harmful_protocols) for startswith. Truthy non-bool values bypass the check and a string protocol list is turned into a tuple of characters.
sum(kappas) sums dict keys, not hidden-degree values, so mean_degree is wrong when kappas is given.
When beta==1 and n==1, math.log(n) is 0 causing division by zero; single-node graph is a valid input.
For n==1 both numerator (1-1/n) and denominator (1-1/n**gam_ratio) are 0, causing ZeroDivisionError.
Generates ordered pairs in both directions (a,b) and (b,a) for symmetric nodes, over-constraining symmetry breaking so valid isomorphisms are pruned.
When graph is empty the largest common induced subgraph is the empty mapping, but code yields nothing instead of {}.
When no candidate sets match, code returns without yielding, but the empty mapping is still the largest common subgraph and should be yielded.
Using `if not notes` treats an empty list as missing, creating a new local list and discarding the env reference. This loses previously stored footnotes and can produce duplicate indices.
`if not indexes` treats an empty dict as missing, causing a rebuild from possibly reset notes and leading to index collisions.
The footnote_ref token uses `raw: key` which is the normalized key, not the original match. The raw should be the original text `m.group(0)`.
`is True` is an identity check and is fragile for boolean values.

`tuple(self._allow_harmful_protocols)` will iterate over characters if the setting is a string and the allowed protocols are never lowercased, so startswith can match any character and bypass the harmful-protocol check.
`os.path.commonpath([source_dir, dest])` raises ValueError when the paths are on different drives, causing an unhandled exception.
The test is inverted: `if os.path.isfile(dest):` returns a 'Could not find file' error when the file exists, and missing files fall through to `open`, causing FileNotFoundError.
Uses `"(" - " ".join(inner)` which raises TypeError instead of parenthesizing nested markers.
sys_tags() returns an iterator, not a Sequence; passing it directly lets the selector exhaust it after the first package so later wheels never match.
frozenset(extras and []) is always empty when extras is given and raises TypeError on frozenset(None) when extras is None, so extra markers never match.
Directly indexes environment["python_full_version"] so a provided partial environment without that key raises KeyError instead of falling back to default_environment().
Raises InvalidVersion when regex matches and then dereferences None.match when it doesn't, so valid versions are rejected and invalid versions crash with AttributeError.

Isinstance against OutEdgeDataView is true for simple DiGraph and false for undirected MultiGraph, so simple directed edges take the multiedge branch and undirected multigraph edges take the simple branch.
Multiedge unpacks thing as 2-tuple (u,v) ignoring the key and passes self.subgraph[u][v] which is dict-of-keys to thing_matcher instead of single edge data.
Same as subgraph side: unpacks 2-tuple and passes dict of parallel edges self.graph[u][v] to thing_matcher, crashes on 3-tuple edge keys.
Alignment lookup uses self.subgraph[sgt[0]][sgt[1]] / self.graph[gt[0]][gt[1]] which is dict of parallel edges and drops the key, so comparison is on wrong object.
For n==1, kappa_0 is 0/0 because (1-1/n) and (1-1/n**gam_ratio) are both 0, raising ZeroDivisionError instead of returning single-node graph.
For beta==1 mu uses log(n) so n==1 divides by zero and n==0 has math domain error; n==0 also crashes on min() and log(n/pi).
Empty string is not quoted so shlex-based reader loses the token and cannot recover original string.
Single-quote is not treated as needing quotes, but shlex splits on single quotes so e.g. "it's" will not round-trip.
Empty platforms list is falsy so `or` substitutes system tags instead of yielding no tags.
Threading is detected from abis including stable abis, so a user-passed abi3t forces threaded mode and wrong abi3t handling.
Major-only python_version has no index 1, so older-version loop raises IndexError when abi3 applies.
Name regex is only checked when '__' in name, so other invalid project names bypass validation.
If the regex does not match, match is None and match.group() raises AttributeError instead of InvalidVersion.
Simple fast-path accepts any digit/dot string, so leading-zero releases like '01' or '1.01' are accepted though PEP 440 forbids them.
Direct subscript environment["python_full_version"] raises KeyError when an environment dict is supplied without that key.
Specifier.contains() defaults to prereleases=False, so pre-release python_full_version is incorrectly rejected for requires_python.
Same missing prereleases=True for per-package requires_python check, incorrectly rejecting pre-releases.
compatible_tags_selector yields (wheel, tags) pairs, but best_wheel tuple is yielded directly instead of the wheel.
Lock-file environments are evaluated with context="requirement" instead of lock-file semantics, changing extras handling.
Uses `tags or sys_tags()` so an explicitly passed empty `tags` sequence falls back to `sys_tags()` instead of meaning no compatible tags.
Uses `parse_wheel_filename(...)[-2]` which is the build tag, not the set of Tags; wheel compatibility then fails or picks wrong wheel.
Uses `parts[2]` for EXT_SUFFIX like `.cpython-310-....so` which yields `so`, losing the ABI; should use the SOABI component.

peek consumes the next element with next(self) and never stores it back in _cache. The index manipulation sets _index to len(_cache)-1 and does not keep the peeked value, so the element is lost and subsequent iteration state is corrupted. peek therefore behaves as next instead of peek.

Iterables are permuted by length descending before interleaving. The output therefore corresponds to the sorted order, not the order the caller passed in. The docstring examples rely on this reordering, but the function contract implies positional identity of iterables is preserved.
With an empty iterables list dims is 0 and lengths_desc[0] is accessed. This raises IndexError, and the error initialization would divide by zero.

count(-1, n) starts slicing at index -1, so the first slice is seq[-1:-1+n] instead of seq[0:n]. For most sequences this yields an empty or wrong slice, causing the takewhile to stop immediately and sliced to return incorrect results.
Using `tags or sys_tags()` treats an explicitly passed empty tag list as unspecified and falls back to the current platform tags, so no wheel should match but current-platform wheels may be selected.
Condition uses `or` instead of `and`: when requires_python is set it always raises even if satisfied, and when it is None it evaluates `None.contains()` causing AttributeError.
Fast path starts search at i+1 where i=start, so an occurrence exactly at start is missed; first yielded index is start+1 at best.
ValueError is suppressed around the whole while True loop. When seq_index raises ValueError the exception is swallowed but the loop repeats with the same i, yielding forever.
errors are initialised positive and only increased by deltas_secondary, so e_ < 0 is never true. Secondary iterators are never yielded and the algorithm does not interleave.
The loop unconditionally does yield next(iter_primary) while to_yield counts sum(lengths). When primary is shorter than the total, next(iter_primary) raises StopIteration.

peek calls next(self) which consumes the Peekable iterator/cache. Repeated peeks advance the underlying iterator and return different items, and the _index manipulation does not preserve the peeked element.

_reconstruct_k_components propagates a k+1 component down to level k only when it is already contained in a k-level component. The comment requires propagation unless it is contained, so the containment test is inverted and the hierarchy is built incorrectly.
new_sg_p is a list and extra is a list; `list(new_sg_p) - extra` uses list subtraction which is not supported in Python and raises TypeError whenever there are unmatched subgraph partitions.
make_qstr only does `t = str(t)` when t is already a str, then checks `" " in t`. For non-string inputs the membership test raises TypeError and the value is never stringified.

Isolated nodes are skipped and k_components[0] is never populated; _reconstruct_k_components loops only down to 1, so connectivity level 0 is never returned despite the docstring stating isolated nodes have connectivity 0.
The loop yields next(iter_primary) on every iteration until sum(lengths) items are produced. iter_primary only contains delta_primary items, so after delta_primary iterations StopIteration is raised.

Errors are initialised to delta_primary//dims and only increased by deltas_secondary each step, and secondary items are yielded only when e_ < 0. Errors are therefore always positive and secondaries are never yielded; the Bresenham accumulation is inverted.
Fast path sets i = start and then searches with seq_index(value, i + 1, stop). The first search therefore starts at start+1, so a match at index start is missed.
With strict=True the code returns a generator that simply yields the same takewhile iterator as non-strict mode and never raises ValueError for a final partial slice.
Continuation indent uses len(name)+1 but header line is `Name: value`, so alignment requires len(name)+2 for `: `. Produces misaligned folded header.

Branch normalizes lhs with canonicalize_name for any op when rhs is in MARKERS_ALLOWING_SET, and applies package-name canonicalization to dependency_groups. Should only normalize `in`/`not in` for `extras`.

Condition requires token == "(" and token == ")" at once, so always False. Missing-operator and empty-parens check never fires, letting e.g. `MIT (Apache-2.0)` compile as Python call and pass as valid.
final_token is lowercased but license_ref_allowed expects `LicenseRef-` prefix case-sensitively, so valid LicenseRefs are rejected and original-case validation is lost.
range(max_k, 0, -0) uses step -0 which is zero, causing ValueError: range() arg 3 must not be zero and crashes _reconstruct_k_components.
sg_match for multiedge unpacks thing1, thing2 as (u1,v1),(u2,v2). For MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph edge identifiers are 3-tuples (u,v,key), so unpacking raises ValueError.
g_match for multiedge has the same 2-tuple unpack assumption as sg_match and will fail for MultiGraph edge identifiers.

For multiedge case sgt_ and gt_ are obtained via self.subgraph[sgt[0]][sgt[1]] / self.graph[gt[0]][gt[1]], which for a MultiGraph returns a dict of parallel edges rather than the specific edge attributes used by thing_matcher.
Multiedge detection only checks isinstance(..., OutEdgeDataView). Undirected MultiGraph edge views are EdgeDataView, so multiedge cases are missed and node/edge handling is mixed.
nx.node_connectivity(C, ...) is called on C = B.subgraph(nodes) without ensuring C has at least two nodes; a 0/1 node subgraph raises NetworkXError.
make_qstr wraps strings containing a space in double quotes but does not escape existing double quotes, producing malformed Pajek strings when the input already contains ".
Uses `platforms or platform_tags()` so an explicit empty iterable incorrectly falls back to system platforms instead of yielding nothing.
Only `abi3` and `none` are removed from explicit abis, so an explicit `abi3t` is yielded twice: once as explicit ABI and once as stable ABI.
Docstring allows major-only `python_version`, but `python_version[1]` raises IndexError if stable-ABI tags apply.
Uses `"(" - " ".join(inner)` which raises TypeError instead of concatenating strings.
Single-wrapper unwrapping drops the `first` flag, so a nested `[[...]]` with `first=False` loses its required parentheses.
mean_degree is computed with sum(kappas) which sums dict keys, not values, so mu and the whole graph are wrong when kappas is supplied.

angle = fabs(pi - fabs(...)) - pi is the negative of the minimal angular distance, so R*angle is <=0. pow of a negative base with non-integer beta raises ValueError and otherwise gives wrong p_ij; p_ij can exceed 1.
R_hat and radii do not follow the documented S1->H2 mapping: R_hat uses log(mu*kappa_min) instead of log(mu*kappa0**2) and radii = R_hat - R_c*log(kappa) instead of R_hat - R_c*log(kappa/kappa0).
new_sg_p = list(new_sg_p) - extra attempts list subtraction, which raises TypeError.
elif self.graph: return exits the generator immediately for any non-empty graph, so largest_common_subgraph never yields mappings.
to_be_mapped = {frozenset(...)} creates a set containing one frozenset instead of a set of nodes, breaking the downstream mapping logic.
The return for a non-first list uses '(' - ' '.join(inner) + ')', attempting string subtraction which raises TypeError and never produces parentheses.
assert isinstance(marker, (list, tuple, str)) does not allow MarkerAtom, so a valid MarkerAtom argument triggers AssertionError despite being in the type hint.
extras=frozenset(extras and []) evaluates to frozenset([]) for any truthy extras and to frozenset(None) for None, so extras are always cleared or TypeError is raised.
env_python_full_version is obtained with 'environment["python_full_version"] if environment else ...', so an explicitly passed empty dict is treated as falsy and falls back to default_environment.
The regex match is inverted: InvalidVersion is raised when match succeeds, and when match is None the code proceeds to match.group causing AttributeError.
token[:-0] is token[:0] which is always empty, so licenses with trailing '+' lose the name.
tokens were lowercased but LicenseRef prefix is case-sensitive, so license_ref_allowed.match on lowercased final_token always fails for valid refs.
WITH is accepted whenever previous output token is WITH, without checking it follows a license id, so '(MIT) WITH exc' is accepted.
variable name compared as == "extra" case-sensitively, so Extra / EXTRA markers are not normalized inconsistently with evaluate.
dependency_groups literals normalized with canonicalize_name which is PEP 503/685 name normalization, inconsistent with dependency-group normalization used by evaluate.
error uses self.raw_name (distribution name) instead of the field name for single-line check.

peek calls next(self) unconditionally and then rewinds _index. If the peeked element is already in the cache the call advances the internal index and the subsequent _index -= 1 does not restore the original iterator state, causing duplicates / skips and an incorrect _index for the next call.

errors are initialised with delta_primary // dims and only increased, and the test is e_ < 0. With positive deltas the test is never true, so secondary iterables are never yielded. The Bresenham error must be accumulated and tested against delta_primary with the opposite sign.

to_yield is set to sum(lengths) and the loop yields next(iter_primary) on every iteration. After the primary iterable is exhausted the loop continues because to_yield still contains the remaining secondary items, leading to StopIteration.

strict=True does not enforce strict slicing. The iterator is built with takewhile(len, ...) which yields a final partial slice, and ret() simply re-yields it without raising ValueError when the sequence length is not a multiple of n.
Charset comparison is case-sensitive, so valid 'utf-8' is rejected while only 'UTF-8' passes.
Tuple (MarkerAtom) case returns early without normalizing, so extra normalization never happens and nested lists are never recursed.
Falls through to `lhs, op, rhs = result` for str operators ('and'/'or'), causing ValueError unpack error or wrong split of 3-char strings.
Condition requires token == '(' and token == ')' at once via `and`, so it is always False and missing-operator and empty-parens checks never fire.
LicenseRef with trailing '+' strips suffix for lookup but license_refs keys include '+', so `license_refs[final_token]` raises KeyError instead of InvalidLicenseExpression.
list subtraction `list(new_sg_p) - extra` is not supported in Python and the logic is inverted; unmatched subgraph partitions should be appended, not removed.
Multiedge `sg_match` unpacks thing as `(u1, v1)` and uses `self.subgraph[u1][v1]` which for a MultiGraph is a dict of parallel edges. The edge key is lost and the matcher receives the wrong object.
`g_match` for multiedges has the same unpacking / attribute access bug as `sg_match`, losing the edge key and passing a dict of parallel edges to `thing_matcher`.
Representative extraction for multiedge case uses `self.subgraph[sgt[0]][sgt[1]]` and `self.graph[gt[0]][gt[1]]`, ignoring the edge key and therefore comparing the wrong data with `thing_matcher`.

Angular distance is computed as `fabs(pi - fabs(...)) - pi`, which is always <=0. `R*angle` is negative, so `math.pow(R*angle, beta)` raises ValueError for non-integer beta and yields wrong connection probabilities otherwise.
The code only does `t = str(t)` when `t` is already a str, leaving non-string inputs unchanged. Subsequent iteration and `.replace` then raise TypeError.

Multiedge sg_match unpacks thing1 as (u1,v1) and uses self.subgraph[u1][v1]; multigraph edge identifiers are (u,v,key) and self.subgraph[u1][v1] is a dict of parallel edges, so the matcher receives the wrong object and will raise or compare incorrectly.
g_match for multiedges has the same unpacking problem as sg_match, using (u1,v1),(u2,v2) and self.graph[u1][v1] which is a dict of parallel edges.

When aligning partitions for multiedges the representative attribute is obtained as self.subgraph[sgt[0]][sgt[1]] / self.graph[gt[0]][gt[1]], i.e. a dict of all parallel edges, instead of the attribute of the specific edge identified by sgt/gt. thing_matcher therefore compares wrong values.

Radial coordinate computation is incorrect: R_hat uses log(mu*kappa_min) instead of log(mu*kappa0**2) and radii are computed as R_hat - R_c*log(kappa) instead of R_hat - R_c*log(kappa/kappa0). This yields wrong 'radius' node attributes.
power = 1/(1-gamma) is used without guarding gamma==1, causing ZeroDivisionError for a valid exponent.

When Ncolors < N extra graph-only partitions are appended to new_g_p but new_sg_p is not padded, so the two returned partition lists have different lengths, breaking the documented aligned-partition contract used by find_isos.
Condition is inverted: valid versions (regex match) raise InvalidVersion while invalid versions fall through to match.group causing AttributeError.
Using `tags or sys_tags()` treats an explicit empty tag list as unspecified and falls back to system tags instead of selecting nothing.
Direct subscript environment["python_full_version"] raises KeyError if a custom environment dict does not contain that key instead of falling back to default.
parse_wheel_filename returns (name, version, build, tags), so [-2] is the build tag not the wheel tags; compatibility check gets wrong data.
If regex fullmatch fails match is None and match.group raises AttributeError instead of InvalidVersion.
Using match() allows trailing invalid characters (e.g. 'foo!') to pass; project name must be fully validated.
int() on build digits can raise ValueError which escapes instead of InvalidWheelFilename.
tags or sys_tags() treats explicit empty list as unspecified, selecting wheels when none should match.
Direct environment["python_full_version"] raises KeyError when a partial environment dict is supplied.
Specifier.contains defaults prereleases to False so prerelease python_full_version is incorrectly rejected.
Same prereleases issue for per-package requires_python check.
Duplicate detection uses raw package.name without normalization so Foo vs foo are not detected as conflict.
if best_wheel: relies on truthiness instead of identity; should test for None.
Uses substring test `content_type not in value.lower()` to detect unparseable type, so any garbage containing e.g. `text/plain` as substring is accepted.
Compares charset case-sensitively to "UTF-8", so valid "utf-8" or "Utf-8" is rejected.
Setting email header with newlines/controls raises ValueError instead of the documented InvalidMetadata error.
Normalizes extra literal for any operator, including `in`/`not in` where the Value is not a single extra name, corrupting substring/container semantics.
Uses `token[:-0]` which is empty string, so any license with `+` suffix becomes unknown/invalid.
Matches lowercased `final_token` against `license_ref_allowed` which expects `LicenseRef-` prefix, so all LicenseRefs fail or must use fullmatch semantics.
Direct dict lookup `license_refs[final_token]` raises KeyError for `LicenseRef-foo+` because key was stored with suffix, crashing instead of raising InvalidLicenseExpression.
Requires exactly two of vcs_info/archive_info/dir_info to be present, but contract requires exactly one.
Unconditionally rejects `.*` suffix instead of only rejecting when operator is not `==` or `!=`, so valid `==1.0.*` is rejected and valid suffix is never consumed.
Unconditionally rejects local version label instead of only rejecting when operator is not `==` or `!=`, so valid `==1.0+local` is rejected and valid suffix is never consumed.
Accepts trailing comma like `==1.0,` by breaking out of loop when no SPECIFIER follows COMMA instead of raising syntax error.
span_end uses `tokenizer.position + 1` while peeked token is not consumed, inconsistent with next check and includes wrong range.
Replaces line boundaries with newline plus header-length padding, corrupting multiline values instead of unfolding to plain newline.
Uses subtraction instead of addition, so archive-only fails validation and all-three-present passes.
Rejects `.*` suffix unconditionally, including valid `==`/`!=` uses; should only reject for other operators.
Rejects local version label unconditionally, including valid `==`/`!=` uses; should only reject for other operators.
Accepts trailing comma like `==1.0,` by breaking loop when no SPECIFIER follows COMMA instead of raising error.
Interpreter is built from python_version[:2] with _version_nodot. For a major-only version e.g. (3,) this yields a malformed 'cp3' tag and does not match the documented major-only behavior.
abi3/abi3t and none tags are emitted even when python_version is major-only. Docstring states major-only should use only user-provided ABIs and the none ABI.
The older-version loop accesses python_version[1] unconditionally, raising IndexError for major-only versions, and also reuses/mutates the interpreter variable.
Formatting of a non-first list uses '(' - ' '.join(inner) + ')', i.e. subtraction of strings, which raises TypeError at runtime.
Assert allows only list/tuple/str but the signature permits MarkerAtom. When a MarkerAtom is passed the assert fails or the else branch returns the raw object instead of a string.
Using `tags or sys_tags()` treats an explicitly passed empty sequence as unspecified and falls back to sys_tags(), yielding wrong wheel selection.
`self.default_groups and []` always evaluates to [] or falsy, so default groups are never used and frozenset(None) can crash.
Direct `environment["python_full_version"]` raises KeyError when a truthy environment dict omits that key, though partial environments are meant to be filled by Marker.evaluate.
`frozenset(extras and [])` discards truthy extras to empty and crashes with frozenset(None) when extras is None.
Direct `environment["python_full_version"]` raises KeyError when a truthy environment dict omits that key, though partial environments are meant to be filled by Marker.evaluate.
`parts[2]` is the file extension (e.g. 'so'), not the SOABI; for '.cpython-310-...-gnu.so' split gives ['', SOABI, 'so'] so ABI becomes 'so'.

@py_random_state(5) passes an integer instead of the seed argument name. NetworkX expects a string name, so the decorator will not correctly manage the random state and can crash or ignore the seed argument.
sum(kappas) iterates over dict keys, not values, so mean_degree is computed from node labels instead of hidden degrees. This propagates to mu and the whole graph.
Radial coordinate mapping uses kappa_min and log(mu*kappa_min) instead of a reference kappa0 and log(mu*kappa0**2) as described in the docstring, yielding incorrect radius values.

For multiedge partitions sg_match accesses self.subgraph[u1][v1]. For MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph this returns a dict of keys->data, not the individual edge data, so thing_matcher receives the wrong object.
g_match for multiedges similarly uses self.graph[u1][v1] which is a dict of edge keys for multigraphs, not the individual edge data.
Representative extraction for multiedge case uses self.subgraph[sgt[0]][sgt[1]] / self.graph[gt[0]][gt[1]] which is a dict of keys for multigraphs, not the edge attribute used by thing_matcher.
to_be_mapped is built as {frozenset(...)} i.e. a set containing one frozenset, instead of a set/frozenset of nodes. Downstream _largest_common_subgraph receives the wrong container type.
The assert only allows list/tuple/str but the type hint includes MarkerAtom. Passing a MarkerAtom instance triggers AssertionError, and the tuple branch assumes .serialize() exists for every element.
first is typed as bool | None = True and is used as a truth test. Passing first=None makes the function treat the call as nested and adds parentheses, producing wrong formatting.

env_python_full_version is derived with `environment["python_full_version"] if environment else ...`. An empty dict is falsy and a non-empty dict missing the key raises KeyError. The check should be `is not None` and use .get with a fallback.

The env dict is built with `environment or {}`. An explicitly passed empty dict is discarded and defaults are used, changing semantics. The same truthiness issue is repeated for the marker evaluation at line 121.

epoch is parsed as `int(match.group("epoch")) if match.group("epoch") else 0`. If the regex captures an empty string the test is truthy and int('') raises ValueError, which is not converted to InvalidVersion.
ext_suffix.split('.') yields ['', abi_part, ext]; parts[2] is the file extension, not the ABI part, so the extracted ABI is wrong and the function returns incorrect tags or a SystemError.
dependency_groups defaults to (self.default_groups and []) which is [] when default_groups is truthy and False/None otherwise; frozenset(False/None) crashes and the default groups are never used.
create_compatible_tags_selector(tags or sys_tags()) treats an empty tags sequence as falsy and substitutes sys_tags(), changing the documented semantics where only None means unspecified.
parse_wheel_filename(wheel.filename)[-2] passes only the ABI tag to compatible_tags_selector instead of the required python/abi/platform tag information, leading to incorrect wheel selection.
The first select version uses parse_wheel_filename(wheel.filename)[-1], which is only the platform tag, so wheel compatibility is evaluated on incomplete data.
A second select method is defined after the first one, shadowing it. The first implementation remains dead code and the file contains two conflicting definitions.
env_python_full_version is obtained via environment["python_full_version"] if environment else ..., which raises KeyError when environment is provided without that key.
Early return for tuple prevents any normalization; lines 10-17 become unreachable for MarkerAtom so extra is never normalized.
Only abi3 and none are removed from explicit abis, so explicit abi3t is yielded twice: once as explicit ABI and once as stable ABI.
platforms or platform_tags() treats explicit empty iterable as missing and substitutes defaults instead of yielding nothing.
python_version[1] crashes with IndexError for major-only version when use_abi3/use_abi3t is true, and doc says major-only must only use user ABIs and none.
Checking only scheme=="file" accepts "file:foo" or "file:path" which are not file:// URLs contrary to error message.
subdirectory is never validated as relative, so absolute path or ../ can escape intended directory.
For SOABI like 'cpython' without '-', split('-')[1] raises IndexError instead of handling the tag.
Substring test 'content_type not in value.lower()' accepts invalid values like 'nottext/plain' because 'text/plain' is a substring.
Charset comparison is case-sensitive, so valid 'utf-8' is rejected though charset names are case-insensitive.
Uses string subtraction '"(" - ...' which raises TypeError for any nested marker.

The requires_python guard uses `or` instead of `and`. With `or` the check is true whenever self.requires_python is truthy, so a matching version still raises PylockSelectError, and when self.requires_python is None the right-hand side is evaluated causing AttributeError on None.contains.

compatible_tags_selector is built with `tags or sys_tags()`. An explicitly passed empty tags sequence is falsy and is therefore replaced by sys_tags(), changing the documented semantics where only `tags is None` should fall back to sys_tags().
Default dependency_groups uses `(self.default_groups and [])` which is always [] when default_groups is truthy and crashes with frozenset(None) when it is None, instead of using the default groups.
Direct indexing environment["python_full_version"] raises KeyError when an environment dict is supplied without that key instead of falling back to default_environment().

Top-level environments markers are evaluated with only `environment or {}` and context="requirement", omitting the extras/dependency_groups set in env and using the wrong context; should use env with context="lock_file".
The parentheses check combines '(' and ')' tests with 'and', requiring token == '(' and token == ')' at the same time, so the condition is never true and invalid parentheses are never rejected.

license_refs is built from the raw split tokens, so a ref like 'LicenseRef-Foo+' is stored under the key 'licenseref-foo+'. Later final_token has the '+' stripped, so license_refs[final_token] raises KeyError for LicenseRef expressions with a '+' suffix.

Lookup license_refs[final_token] is performed after final_token has been stripped of '+', which does not match the dict key that was created from the un-stripped token, causing a KeyError for LicenseRef+.
Continuation indentation is computed as len(name)+1, which is one space short for RFC 822 folding where the continuation should align after 'Name: ' i.e. len(name)+2 spaces.
lhs, op, rhs = result unpacks without checking length, so a tuple that is not a 3-element marker expression raises ValueError.

The regex match test is inverted: `if match:` raises InvalidVersion for a successful match and allows execution to continue when match is None. This rejects every valid PEP 440 version and causes AttributeError on `match.group` for invalid versions.

Wheel filename parsing counts dashes and splits left with `filename.split('-', dashes-2)`. Project names containing hyphens increase dash count and cause the left split to allocate parts of the name to version/build/tag, so names with dashes are mis-parsed or rejected.

Wheel selection passes `parse_wheel_filename(wheel.filename)[-2]` to `compatible_tags_selector`. Index -2 is the build tag, not the tag set. The selector therefore receives build information instead of tags and will never find a compatible wheel.

env_python_full_version is obtained with `environment["python_full_version"] if environment else ...`. An empty dict is falsy and a non-empty dict missing the key raises KeyError, so a partial environment dict crashes the selector.

The check sums bool(vcs_info)+bool(archive_info)+bool(dir_info) and raises if !=2, but the error message requires exactly one of the three to be present. This allows two infos and rejects the valid single-info case.

After consuming optional WS and reading a COMMA the parser does not verify that a SPECIFIER follows. A trailing comma is therefore accepted and appended to parsed_specifiers, producing an invalid spec string.

Whitespace around commas is consumed with tokenizer.consume('WS') but never appended to parsed_specifiers. The returned string loses the original WS between specifiers, so the reconstructed specifier list is not faithful to the source.

The syntax error for VERSION_PREFIX_TRAIL uses span_end=tokenizer.position + 1 while the analogous VERSION_LOCAL_LABEL_TRAIL error uses span_end=tokenizer.position. The +1 makes the span inconsistent/off-by-one.
Condition is inverted: valid versions match the regex but code raises InvalidVersion when match succeeds, and then dereferences None for invalid versions.
Code unconditionally raises on `.*` trail, rejecting valid `==1.0.*` and `!=1.0.*` specifiers instead of only rejecting bad operators or pre/post/dev/local versions.
Code unconditionally rejects local version label, even with `==` or `!=` operators where it is allowed.
Two mutually exclusive `token ==` checks joined with `and` can never be true, so missing-operator-before-`(` and empty `()` checks are dead code.
license_refs keys include trailing `+` but lookup at line 194 uses stripped final_token, so `LicenseRef-Foo+` causes KeyError instead of normalized expression.
Any `.*` suffix unconditionally raises, so valid `==1.*` / `!=1.*` are rejected and the trail token is never consumed.
Any local-label trail unconditionally raises, so valid `==1.0+local` / `!=1.0+local` are rejected and the token is never consumed.
If regex does not match, `match` is None and `match.group` raises AttributeError instead of documented InvalidVersion.
Fast path accepts any digit-dot string, so invalid versions with leading zeros like `01` or `1.02` are accepted instead of raising InvalidVersion.
`token[:-0]` equals `token[:0]` == "", so `+` handling empties final_token and valid `MIT+` raises Unknown license.
`license_refs` keys are built with trailing `+` included, so lookup of stripped `final_token` for `LicenseRef-... +` raises KeyError instead of InvalidLicenseExpression.
Uses parse_wheel_filename(...)[-2] which is the build tag, not the tags set, so wheel compatibility is evaluated against wrong data.
`extras and []` is always falsy-empty and raises TypeError via frozenset(None) when extras is None, so requested extras are never applied.
Only rejects "\n" in Summary, allowing "\r" to pass through as a line break / header injection.
token[:-0] always returns '' so a license token ending with '+' is stripped to empty. The lookup for the license/exception then fails or raises a wrong error, breaking '+' suffix handling.
lhs, op, rhs = result assumes result is a 3-element tuple. If a marker tuple has a different arity the unpack raises ValueError.
For a list input the function returns a plain list comprehension, losing the original MarkerList type. Callers expecting the same type will break.

Interpreter is built from python_version[:2] without ensuring a minor version is present. For a major-only python_version the slice is length 1, producing a malformed cpX interpreter and later code that indexes python_version[1] will raise IndexError.

The older-version loop evaluates range(python_version[1] - 1, ...) and accesses python_version[0], python_version[1] without verifying len(python_version) >= 2. With a major-only version this raises IndexError even when the loop body would be skipped.

Dash counting on the stripped filename includes dashes that belong to the distribution name. The check dashes in (4,5) and split with maxsplit dashes-2 therefore mis-parses names containing dashes and raises InvalidWheelFilename incorrectly or parses name/version incorrectly.
Name validation only raises when '__' is present and the regex fails. An invalid name without '__' will pass validation, violating the wheel name rules.
build_match.group(2) can be None when the optional build suffix is absent, producing a BuildTag tuple containing None instead of a string.

InvalidTag is caught and re-raised as InvalidWheelFilename with the message about empty tag components. InvalidTag can be raised for reasons other than an empty component, giving a misleading error message.
Validation of exactly one of vcs_info, archive_info, dir_info uses bool() sums. Falsy but present objects would be counted as absent, allowing zero or multiple infos to pass validation incorrectly.
self._regex.fullmatch can return None for a non-PEP 440 version, but the code proceeds to call match.group, raising AttributeError instead of InvalidVersion.
_wheel_name_regex.match allows a partial match, so a project name with a valid prefix followed by illegal characters would be accepted.
Counting dashes and splitting with dashes-2 assumes the project name contains no dashes. Names with dashes shift the split boundaries, producing wrong name/version/build/tag parsing.
tags or sys_tags() treats an empty sequence as falsy, so an explicitly passed empty tags list falls back to sys_tags() instead of using the empty selection.
env_python_full_version accesses environment['python_full_version'] when environment is a truthy empty dict, causing KeyError; the same pattern is used for environment markers.
Empty tags list is falsy so `tags or sys_tags()` incorrectly falls back to system tags instead of selecting for no compatible tags.
Uses `or` instead of `and`; when requires_python is None it evaluates None.contains causing AttributeError, and when set the condition is always true.
Directly indexes environment["python_full_version"] when any truthy environment is passed, raising KeyError if that key is missing instead of falling back to default.
Same KeyError: truthy environment dict without python_full_version key crashes instead of using default environment value.
Only folds `\n`, leaving lone `\r` or `\r\n` unhandled, allowing header injection / malformed email output.
Summary check only rejects `\n`, so a value containing `\r` passes and can inject new header lines when serialized.

The expression bool(vcs_info) - bool(archive_info) + bool(dir_info) != 1 does not enforce exactly one info. It accepts the case vcs_info, archive_info and dir_info all present because 1-1+1 == 1, and it rejects archive_info alone.
After consuming a COMMA the loop continues and exits when the next token is not SPECIFIER, leaving a trailing comma in parsed_specifiers. A trailing comma should be a syntax error.
Error span for VERSION_PREFIX_TRAIL uses span_end=tokenizer.position + 1, which points past the start of the offending token and is inconsistent with the rest of the parser.

message["content-type"] returns a str from EmailMessage, so .params raises AttributeError. The code then cannot read charset/variant.
variant is taken from params as-is and compared case-sensitively to {'GFM','CommonMark'}. A valid lowercase variant like 'gfm' is rejected.

Normalization is only applied to the top-level tuple. Nested tuples/lists inside lhs/rhs are not recursively normalized, so extras deep in an expression stay uncanonicalized.
When a token ends with '+', final_token is set to token[:-0] which is always ''. This empties the license identifier and causes Unknown license / KeyError.
