Uses `[-2]` (build tag) instead of `[-1]` (tags set) from parse_wheel_filename, so wheel compatibility is evaluated on wrong data.
Condition requires `__` to check project name, so empty names and other invalid names without `__` slip through instead of raising InvalidWheelFilename.
Uses `self.default_groups and []` which is always empty/falsy, so default groups are never selected.
Direct indexing `environment["python_full_version"]` crashes with KeyError when a partial environment is given; Marker.evaluate is documented to fill missing keys.
Only "\n" is folded, bare "\r" is left in the value allowing header injection / malformed email.
Checks only "\n", so a Summary containing bare "\r" bypasses single-line validation.
Substring test `content_type not in value.lower()` accepts invalid values like "text/plain bogus" that contain a valid type.
Case-sensitive `charset != "UTF-8"` rejects valid "utf-8" / "Utf-8".
Tuple (MarkerAtom) returns early unnormalized making lines 70-87 dead code, while str connectors like "and"/"or" fall through to `lhs,op,rhs=result` corrupting/crashing.
token[:-0] is token[:0] which is empty, so any version with trailing + loses the license id and is always rejected.
license_refs keys/values are built with trailing + still attached, so lookup by stripped final_token raises KeyError and value would double the +.
Sum of present info objects is compared to 2 instead of 1, rejecting valid direct_url and accepting two infos present.
.* suffix raises unconditionally without checking operator, so valid ==1.0.* and !=1.0.* are rejected.
Local version label raises unconditionally without checking operator, so valid ==/!= with +local are rejected.
VERSION_PREFIX_TRAIL and VERSION_LOCAL_LABEL_TRAIL are only peeked, never consumed/appended, so valid suffixes are dropped from parsed_specifiers and left in tokenizer.
span_end uses tokenizer.position without trail length, producing zero-length span for local label error.
Exception message uses lower-cased token instead of original case, contradicting documented 'Unknown license' example.
Unknown license message uses lower-cased final_token, so 'Use-it-after-midnight' is reported as 'use-it-after-midnight'.
Uses ` - bool(archive_info)` instead of `+`, so a lone archive_info gives -1 !=1 and is wrongly rejected.
Raises for `.*` suffix unconditionally, rejecting valid `==1.0.*` and `!=1.0.*` which should be allowed.
Raises for local-version `+` suffix unconditionally, rejecting valid `==`/`!=` uses which should be allowed.
Accepts trailing comma like `==1.0,` because loop returns after consuming COMMA without requiring another SPECIFIER.
LicenseRef with `+` suffix causes KeyError: license_refs keys include `+` but lookup uses stripped final_token.
Matches lowercased final_token against license_ref_allowed, so case-sensitive `LicenseRef-` prefix never matches.
Allows `WITH` chained after an exception like `MIT WITH E1 WITH E2` because it only checks previous normalized token is WITH.
Charset comparison is case-sensitive: charset != "UTF-8" rejects valid 'utf-8' values returned by EmailMessage params.
Variant from parameters is checked against {'GFM','CommonMark'} without normalising case, so 'gfm'/'commonmark' are incorrectly rejected.
Tuple inputs are returned unchanged, so MarkerAtom tuples are never processed and extras are not canonicalized.
Function signature allows str but code does lhs, op, rhs = result, which raises ValueError/TypeError for string inputs and for non-3-element tuples.
Parentheses validation combines the '(' and ')' checks with 'and', requiring token to be both '(' and ')', so the check is dead and invalid parentheses are never raised.
license_refs is built from tokens that may include a trailing '+', but later lookup uses final_token with '+' stripped, causing KeyError for LicenseRef+ expressions.
Date/time overload returns DATE+TIME early and silently drops the optional zone argument handled only in the component path.
pop()/set() mutate the input TimestampFromParts in place so repeated generation gives different results and corrupts the caller's AST.
Raises an error when an analyzer name was successfully parsed and stays silent when it is missing; condition is backwards.
Direct dict lookup crashes with KeyError if the single-column PRIMARY KEY references a missing/mismatched-case/non-column expression.
Params and args are swapped: anon_func.expressions are the first parentheses (params) but are kept as expressions while the second parentheses are stored as params.
Resolved suffix/combiner in parts is never stored on the new instance, so ClickHouse suffixes like -If/-State are lost.
Invalid JSON path is silently swallowed and original path returned even when STRICT_JSON_PATH_SYNTAX is set; warning only for lax/strict prefix.
len==2 branch discards indexes[1] and len==1 single subscript is wrapped in JSONPathUnion; logic is inverted.
Empty union element (trailing comma or double comma like [0,] or [0,,1]) is silently skipped instead of raising ParseError.
Counting dashes and splitting with dashes-2 assumes the distribution name contains no dashes, so names with dashes are split incorrectly and name/version/tag are extracted wrong.
Build presence is inferred from dashes == 5, which is false when the distribution name itself contains dashes. This mis-identifies the build part and the tag string.
dependency_groups default uses (self.default_groups and []) which evaluates to [] whenever default_groups is truthy, so the default groups are discarded instead of being used.
env_python_full_version accesses environment["python_full_version"] directly; if a non-empty dict is passed without that key a KeyError is raised.
create_compatible_tags_selector(tags or sys_tags()) treats an explicitly passed empty tags sequence as falsy and falls back to sys_tags(), changing the selection result.

When dependency_groups is None the code uses (self.default_groups and []) which returns [] when default_groups is truthy and returns self.default_groups (often None) otherwise. This discards the default groups and can make frozenset(None) raise TypeError.
extras=frozenset(extras and []) discards any provided extras – extras and [] is [] for truthy extras – and passes None to frozenset when extras is None, raising TypeError.

EXT_SUFFIX is split on '.' with a leading empty element, so the ABI component is parts[1]. The code checks len(parts) < 3 and then uses soabi = parts[2], which for '.cpython-310-x86_64-linux-gnu.so' yields 'so' instead of the ABI string, producing wrong or empty ABI tags.
A second select method is defined after the first one, silently overwriting it. The first implementation is dead code and the duplicate definition hides the intended change.
sample from self.sql has no leading space, so pre_alias/post_alias concatenate directly with table/alias/pivots producing invalid SQL like tblTABLESAMPLE.
ordinality containing the alias is appended after joins/laterals/hints/pivots, so a table with ordinality plus join renders WITH ORDINALITY last instead of immediately after the table.
Condition wraps when parent is in WRAPPED_JSON_EXTRACT_EXPRESSIONS, causing double parentheses, instead of skipping wrap when parent already wraps.
or with date_part_boundary forces DAY subtraction for any unit, ignoring requested unit like MONTH/YEAR.
EXTRACT(days FROM interval) returns only the days component, dropping months/years, so WEEK is wrong for intervals over a month.
The regex match test is inverted: an InvalidVersion is raised when match succeeds and parsing continues with a possibly None match, causing crashes and accepting invalid versions.

The parentheses validation uses `and` between the '(' check and the ')' check, requiring a token to be both '(' and ')'. The condition is therefore never true and invalid parenthesis placements are never detected.

license_refs is built from the raw tokens including a trailing '+' suffix, but later lookup uses final_token with the suffix stripped. A LicenseRef token that itself carries '+' will cause a KeyError.
tokenizer.check is called with keyword argument peek=True. The Tokenizer.check API does not accept a peek parameter, so this will raise TypeError / is a misuse; the same misuse occurs at line 25.
When VERSION_PREFIX_TRAIL is present the error message is swapped: the message for allowed '=='/ '!=' operators is used for the disallowed case and vice-versa, leading to misleading diagnostics.
MarkerAtom is a 3-tuple. Returning the tuple unchanged prevents any extra name canonicalisation and also prevents recursion into its lhs/rhs.
After the list/tuple guards the code unconditionally does lhs, op, rhs = result. For a str input or for a tuple of wrong length this raises ValueError/TypeError.
interpreter is built from python_version[:2]. With a major-only version the slice is length 1, so _version_nodot produces a malformed cp tag.
The older-version loop accesses python_version[1] and builds (python_version[0], minor_version) without checking that python_version has at least two components. Major-only versions raise IndexError.
interpreter is reassigned inside the minor-version loop, clobbering the outer interpreter variable and making the code fragile / confusing.

Exactly-one check uses bool(direct_url.vcs_info)+bool(direct_url.archive_info)+bool(direct_url.dir_info). An empty but present object is falsy and will be mis-counted; presence should be tested with is not None.
pre_alias/post_alias built from sample/version have no leading space and no separator between them, so output becomes e.g. `tblTABLESAMPLE...` when partition/file_format are empty.
Merging alias into ordinality which is emitted last in line 64 moves the alias after hints/pivots/joins/laterals instead of right after the table.
Casting both sides to TIMESTAMP drops time zone and precision, giving wrong results for TIMESTAMPTZ or DATE/TIME inputs.
EXTRACT(days FROM (end-start)) returns only the days field of the interval, ignoring months/years, so WEEK diff is wrong across month boundaries.
factor from DATE_DIFF_FACTOR on line 85 is never used; DAY/HOUR/MINUTE/SECOND etc fall through to CAST(AGE(...) AS BIGINT) which is an interval-to-bigint cast and fails/is wrong.
QUARTER (and WEEK) division truncates toward zero on CAST to BIGINT instead of flooring, giving wrong results for negative intervals; also needs FLOOR.
Return statement uses "(" - " ".join(inner) + ")" with a subtraction operator instead of concatenation, causing a SyntaxError and preventing module import.
Type hint allows MarkerAtom but assert only permits list, tuple, str, so a valid MarkerAtom input raises AssertionError.
raise ... from defect uses a policy defect object which is not a BaseException, so the raise itself raises TypeError.
Charset comparison is case-sensitive; a valid 'utf-8' value is rejected because it is not equal to 'UTF-8'.
Markdown variant check is case-sensitive, so values like 'gfm' or 'commonmark' are incorrectly rejected.
PyPy ABI is built with hyphens, e.g. 'pypy38-pp73', while the documented tag uses underscores 'pypy38_pp73'.
GraalPy ABI is built with hyphens, e.g. 'graalpy-38-native', while the documented tag uses underscores 'graalpy_38_native'.
tags or sys_tags() treats an explicitly empty tags sequence as falsy and falls back to sys_tags(), ignoring the caller request.
environment["python_full_version"] is accessed directly; a provided environment dict missing that key raises KeyError.
compatible_tags_selector is fed parse_wheel_filename(...)[-2], which is the build tag, not the tags set. Wheel selection will use the wrong value.
filename.split("-", dashes-2) splits from the left, so a distribution name containing dashes is split apart and name/version are mis-parsed.

dependency_groups default is built as (self.default_groups and []) which is [] when default_groups is truthy and None when it is None, so default groups are lost and frozenset(None) can raise TypeError.
Same environment["python_full_version"] direct access as in the first select; a provided environment missing the key crashes with KeyError.
select is defined twice in the same module; the second definition silently overrides the first, making the first version dead code and the file confusing.

extras is built as frozenset(extras and []). For a truthy extras it evaluates to frozenset([]) so extras are always dropped, and for extras is None it evaluates to frozenset(None) which raises TypeError. The intended default is an empty collection, not an empty-forced one.

Wheel compatibility is checked with parse_wheel_filename(wheel.filename)[-1]. The first version of select used [-2]; changing the index selects a different component of the parsed wheel filename, so the compatible_tags_selector is given the wrong tag and wheel selection is incorrect.

create_compatible_tags_selector(tags or sys_tags()) treats an explicitly passed empty tags sequence as falsy and silently falls back to sys_tags(). The documented contract is to fall back only when tags is None.

VERSION_PREFIX_TRAIL is always treated as an error. The code raises a syntax error unconditionally when a .* trail is present, instead of raising only when the operator is not ==/!= or the version is pre/post/dev/local. This makes every .* specifier invalid.
span_end is computed as tokenizer.position + 1 after reading the specifier. The +1 shifts the end of the reported span past the actual token.
The syntax error for VERSION_LOCAL_LABEL_TRAIL uses span_end = tokenizer.position, which points to the start of the trail token rather than its end, giving an incorrect source span.

After the simple-version fast path, self._regex.fullmatch(version) can return None. The code immediately accesses match.group(...), causing AttributeError instead of raising InvalidVersion as documented.
final_token = token[:-0] always produces an empty string. The trailing '+' is never removed, so look-ups for licenses/licenserefs use '' and crash with KeyError.

The SPDX 'with' exception operator is replaced with 'or' when building a Python expression for syntax checking. This changes the logical meaning of the expression and can accept invalid or reject valid license expressions.
Condition is inverted: when `(VALUES` was consumed `is_derived` is True, code then requires another VALUES/FORMAT VALUES and returns None, and when no VALUES keyword exists it still parses values.
Laterals are never generated because `x and []` is always empty; should be `or`.
If no ALTERABLE matches, `alter_token` is False/None but `.token_type` is accessed, raising AttributeError.
Same crash when ALTER target is missing; `alter_token.token_type` assumes a match.
Advances only if `self._next` exists, so a final action keyword in `_curr` is never moved to `_prev` for parser lookup.
Alter is only returned when `not self._curr`; any trailing token/semicolon or next statement forces fallback to Command, discarding parsed Alter.
Calls `_parse_table_alias()` twice, risking consuming tokens after a failed first parse.
`LOCAL` is parsed but only stored for DIRECTORY case, so `INSERT LOCAL ...` loses the flag in `exp.Insert`.
Early return for FIRST/ALL multitable inserts drops hint/overwrite/ignore/local/alternative parsed before.
Wrap condition is inverted: it wraps when parent already wraps and skips wrap when it should wrap. Should require not same_parent and parent not wrapped.
If no ALTERABLE matches, alter_token is falsy and alter_token.token_type crashes. ICEBERG path dereferences it unguarded.
Same missing guard: alter_token.token_type crashes when ALTER has no alterable token.
Checks _next instead of _curr, so a final action keyword with no tokens after it is never consumed and parser lookup uses the wrong token.
X.upper() and "DAY" is always "DAY" when unit present and empty when missing. Default logic requires or, so every diff is computed as DAY.
EXTRACT(days FROM interval) returns the day field, not total days, so intervals >=1 month give wrong WEEK diff.
Fallback casts an interval AGE() directly to BIGINT which Postgres cannot cast, producing invalid SQL for DAY/unknown units.

Requires-python check uses `or` instead of `and`. With `or` the condition is true whenever self.requires_python is truthy and also tries to access .contains on None, causing spurious errors or AttributeError.
Compatible tags selector is created with `tags or sys_tags()`. An empty sequence is falsy so an explicit empty tags request is silently replaced by sys_tags().

env_python_full_version is obtained by direct indexing `environment["python_full_version"] if environment else ...`. An empty dict is treated as missing and a provided dict lacking the key raises KeyError.
Same direct indexing of environment for python_full_version in the second select implementation, with the same KeyError / empty-dict edge case.

header_store_parse folds newlines with `" " * (len(name)+2)` spaces. Continuation lines should start with a single whitespace; the calculated size produces excessive indentation and is not the standard RFC 822 folding.
prefer_sdist_predicate is called with `package.name`. The parameter type is Callable[[NormalizedName], bool]; raw package.name may be un-normalized, leading to mismatched predicate results.
Component form TIMESTAMP_FROM_PARTS(year, month, ...) also has `this` (year) and `expression` (month) non-None, so it is misclassified as the date+time form and generates `year + month`.
The `or` makes every unit with `date_part_boundary` use DATE subtraction (days), and makes every DAY use DATE subtraction even when complete 24h days are required.
Assumes the single PRIMARY KEY expression is a plain column present in `defs`; ordered/indexed expressions or unknown columns cause wrong lookup or KeyError.
Unconditionally appends a column PRIMARY KEY constraint even if the column already has one, producing duplicate PRIMARY KEY constraints.
Condition is inverted: it returns None when derived `(VALUES` was matched and proceeds when no VALUES keyword exists. It also already consumed tokens before returning None without retreat.
When not derived and no VALUES keyword, it still parses CSV as Values, stealing SELECT/DDL source and blocking _parse_ddl_select.
Parses table alias twice: alias or self._parse_table_alias() can consume a second alias or ON CONFLICT / RETURNING token as alias.
Keeps full suffixed name in this instead of base name from resolved parts, so Combined/Parameterized agg keeps suffix duplicated.
When expr is Window and params exist, old window parsed before params is kept between params and args instead of re-parsing window after full call.
Appends target.this instead of target, dropping column wrapping and breaking INSERT...SET with qualified or quoted columns.
`expression.args.get("laterals") and []` evaluates to None when key is missing causing TypeError on iteration, and to [] when laterals exist so laterals are never rendered.
`if literal:` drops falsy but valid slice values like index 0 and silently accepts parse failure (False) instead of erroring.
parts is assumed to have three elements and parts[2] is accessed unconditionally, which raises IndexError if _resolve_clickhouse_agg returns a shorter tuple.
`isinstance(literal, str) or literal is not False` is true for any value except False, so ints, None, etc. are accepted as a bracket literal.
When a comma is matched the next slice is parsed but if it is False it is silently skipped, leaving consumed tokens unrepresented and mis-aligning the parse.
For len(indexes)==2 the code builds a node from indexes[0] only, discarding indexes[1] entirely.

ParseError/TokenError from parse_json_path is caught and only logged when STRICT_JSON_PATH_SYNTAX and the text starts with lax/strict; otherwise the error is silently swallowed and the original Literal is returned.
HeaderDefect is not a BaseException. Raising _invalid_metadata with cause=defect and `from defect` will raise TypeError at runtime when a defect is present.

MarkerAtom is a 3-tuple. The early `if isinstance(result, tuple): return result` returns the atom unchanged, so the extra-canonicalisation code below is never executed for atoms and extras stay un-normalised.

The function signature allows str, but after the list/tuple guards it does `lhs, op, rhs = result`. For a str this unpacks characters and for any non-3-item value it raises ValueError, breaking the contract.
Charset comparison is case-sensitive. `parameters.get` can yield 'utf-8' while the check requires 'UTF-8', causing a valid UTF-8 declaration to be rejected.
Variant from email parameters is compared case-sensitively against {'GFM','CommonMark'}. A value like 'gfm' would be rejected even though it is semantically valid.
`x and ""` is always falsy, so `if ordinality:` is never true and `WITH ORDINALITY` is never generated.
Direct dict lookup raises KeyError if the single-column PRIMARY KEY references a column not in `defs`.
Appends a PrimaryKeyColumnConstraint without checking if the column already has one, producing duplicate PRIMARY KEY constraints.
`text(...).upper() and "DAY"` evaluates to "DAY" for any non-empty unit and "" when empty, destroying the unit and the default.
EXTRACT(days FROM interval) returns only the days component, ignoring months/years, so WEEK diff is wrong for large intervals.
token[:-0] is token[:0] i.e. empty string, so a trailing '+' is not removed. final_token becomes '' causing wrong license lookup or KeyError and incorrect normalization.

license_refs is built from the raw split tokens which may include a trailing '+'. Later the token is stripped of '+' before lookup, so license_refs[final_token] misses entries for LicenseRef identifiers with '+', leading to KeyError or missed normalization.

The validation checks bool(vcs_info)+bool(archive_info)+bool(dir_info) != 2 but the error message requires exactly one of the three to be present. The check therefore rejects valid inputs with one field and accepts invalid combos with two fields.
sample is assigned to pre_alias/post_alias without a leading space, so the sample clause is concatenated directly to the preceding token.
ordinality absorbs alias via f" WITH ORDINALITY{alias}" and alias is cleared, but ordinality is appended at the very end of the return string after joins/laterals, breaking correct table syntax.
When indexed is True the code calls self.sql(indexed), which will try to render a boolean as SQL and can raise or produce wrong output.
expression.same_parent is not a valid attribute/method on sqlglot expressions, so the condition is erroneous and may raise AttributeError.
DATE_DIFF_FACTOR.get(unit) is computed into factor but never used, so unit-specific scaling is lost.
For units not handled explicitly the code returns CAST(AGE(...) AS BIGINT). AGE returns an interval, which cannot be cast to BIGINT in Postgres.
Quarter calculation uses EXTRACT(year)*4 + EXTRACT(month)/3, which yields fractional quarters and is not equivalent to total months // 3.
WEEK uses EXTRACT(days FROM (end - start)), which returns only the days component of the interval, not total days, giving wrong week counts for intervals spanning months/years.
Uses `and []` instead of `or []`, so laterals are never generated; truthy list yields empty list.
Passes an instance `exp.Properties(...)` to `self.expression` which expects a class, causing crash/wrong node.
If no ALTERABLE matches, `alter_token` is False and `.token_type` dereference crashes.
Advances only if `self._next` exists, so a trailing action token in `_curr` is never consumed/parsed.
Uses truthiness `if literal:` so index 0 in a union like [1,0] is dropped.
Condition `len(indexes)==2` is inverted; single index becomes Union and two indexes collapse to single node dropping second index and typing by wrong element.
LOCAL is consumed unconditionally but only used for DIRECTORY inserts, so non-DIRECTORY INSERTs silently swallow a stray LOCAL.
Partition clause matches PARTITION_BY instead of PARTITION, so INSERT ... PARTITION (...) is never parsed.
Condition requires a second VALUES after '(VALUES' and proceeds without VALUES when not derived, consuming tokens then returning None without rollback.
OR applies DATE subtraction for any unit when date_part_boundary is set, instead of only for DAY units.
EXTRACT(days FROM interval) returns only the days component, not total days, so WEEK is wrong for intervals over a month.
Fallback casts AGE() interval directly to BIGINT, which Postgres cannot cast.
sample has no leading space while version does, so pre_alias/post_alias concatenation glues TABLESAMPLE to table/alias.
WITH ORDINALITY with alias is appended after joins/laterals instead of immediately after table alias.
Suffix info from _resolve_clickhouse_agg in parts is never stored; instance keeps full anon_func.this name so combined/parameterized aggs regenerate incorrectly.
When super parsed a Window, cursor is after the window spec, so _parse_func_params parses trailing tokens instead of tokens between func call and window.
lax/strict prefix check is case-sensitive and matches any word starting with lax/strict, so valid upper-case prefixes warn and invalid words like laxative suppress warning.
Condition is inverted: raises error when analyzer was successfully parsed and silently accepts missing analyzer name.
expression has no attribute same_parent; accessing it raises AttributeError and the wrap decision is wrong.
_match_set returns a bool, so alter_token can be False. Accessing alter_token.token_type then raises AttributeError when ICEBERG is matched but no ALTERABLE is found.
Same alter_token problem: when alter_token is falsy, `alter_token.token_type == TokenType.SESSION` crashes.
Unconditional `self._advance()` when `self._next` exists discards the next token, causing the first ALTER action to be skipped.

The while condition uses `self._match(TokenType.COMMA) or self._prev.token_type == TokenType.COMMA`. If the match fails, self._prev is stale, so the test can be true incorrectly and the loop can misbehave.

`unit = expression.text("unit").upper() and "DAY"` uses `and` instead of `or`. For a truthy unit the expression evaluates to "DAY", so any specified unit is forced to DAY, and .upper() can raise on None.
Early return for FIRST/ALL multitable inserts drops hint, overwrite, ignore and local parsed above.
Matches PARTITION_BY but Hive/Spark INSERT uses PARTITION (...) so partition clause is never parsed.
SETTINGS is matched before the SELECT/VALUES expression so trailing ClickHouse SETTINGS after the query is missed.
DATE_DIFF_FACTOR is fetched but never used; DAY/HOUR/MINUTE/SECOND fall through to CAST(interval AS BIGINT) which is invalid.
WEEK uses EXTRACT(days FROM end-start) which returns only the days component, dropping months/years.
WITH ORDINALITY is appended after joins/laterals instead of directly after the table/alias.
ROWS FROM overwrites table, discarding WHEN already merged into table and incorrectly keeping ONLY prefix.
Invalid paths starting with lax/strict silently swallow ParseError/TokenError with no warning even when STRICT_JSON_PATH_SYNTAX is set.
Raises when an analyzer was found and stays silent when it is missing, opposite of the error message.
Uses 'and []' instead of 'or []', so present laterals are dropped and missing laterals crashes iterating None.
sample is assigned to pre_alias/post_alias without a leading space, so it concatenates directly to the preceding token e.g. ')TABLESAMPLE' instead of ') TABLESAMPLE'.
ordinality is appended at the very end of the return string after joins/laterals, placing WITH ORDINALITY in the wrong position relative to the table reference.
When indexed is a boolean True the code executes self.sql(indexed), which expects an Expression and will raise.
For an unrecognised unit the code sets unit to the AGE interval and emits CAST(... AS BIGINT), which is invalid SQL in Postgres.
expression.same_parent is used as an attribute for parent checking; the API does not provide this semantics and the wrapping condition is incorrect.
rows_from overwrites the table variable after when and changes have already been applied to table, discarding those modifiers.
QUARTER calculation uses EXTRACT(month FROM age) / 3 producing a fractional value that is truncated by the final CAST to BIGINT.
Laterals are never rendered because `expression.args.get('laterals') and []` evaluates to [] when laterals is truthy, so the comprehension iterates over an empty list.
After matching `( VALUES`, the guard `if is_derived and not (match_text_seq('VALUES') or match_text_seq('FORMAT','VALUES'))` returns None, discarding normal derived VALUES.
Alias is parsed at line 115 and then parsed again in the Values constructor with `alias or self._parse_table_alias()`, causing a second parse that can consume the next token.
alter_token is `False` when `_match_set` fails, yet `alter_token.token_type` is accessed at lines 176 and 182, leading to AttributeError.
Unconditional `self._advance()` consumes the next token regardless of its kind, potentially discarding the ALTER action keyword.
For INSERT ... SET, `_parse_table_alias()` is called when building the Values node, consuming a token from the following clause because SET syntax has no alias.
Lookup assumes PK column exists in defs; dangling or quoted/case-mismatched PK name raises KeyError.
Moves table-level single-column PK to column without checking if column already has a PrimaryKeyColumnConstraint, creating duplicate PK.
Multi-path handling only for exp.JSONExtract; JSONExtractScalar / JSONBExtract with several paths falls through and loses extra paths.
Multi-path early return bypasses same_parent / WRAPPED parenthesization applied below, so nested use can have wrong precedence.
Uses truthiness `if literal:` so falsy indexes like 0 are dropped and empty segments like [1,,2] are silently skipped instead of error.
len(indexes)==2 branch builds node with only indexes[0], discarding second index/bound, and decides type from `literal` instead of the relevant element.
Single-element bracket e.g. [0] falls into else and creates JSONPathUnion with one element instead of subscript/key.

View branch accesses expression.args["alias"] with direct key access and then alias.name without a null guard. If alias is missing or None a KeyError / AttributeError is raised and self.expressions(alias, ...) will also fail.

When ordinality is present the code builds ordinality = f" WITH ORDINALITY{alias}" and clears alias, so the output becomes "WITH ORDINALITY AS alias" instead of the correct "AS alias WITH ORDINALITY".
The comprehension uses expression.args.get("laterals") and [] which evaluates to [] whenever laterals is truthy, so laterals are never emitted.
Condition `isinstance(literal, str) or literal is not False` treats None and other non-False values as valid, allowing a None literal to create a JSONPath node with this=None.
Appending uses `if literal:` which drops valid falsy literals such as 0 or empty string from a comma-separated union.
`expression.args.get("ordinality") and ""` evaluates to `""` (falsy) when ordinality is truthy, so `if ordinality:` is never true and WITH ORDINALITY is never generated.
`self.expression()` expects an expression class, not an instance; passing `instance` raises TypeError / produces wrong node.
Generator detaches `milli`/`nano` via `pop()` and does `expression.set("sec", sec)`, mutating the caller's expression so re-generation or reuse sees corrupted AST.
milli is a list from expression args; milli.pop() mutates the original args and raises IndexError if the list is empty, and discards extra values.
nano.pop() mutates expression args and can raise IndexError on an empty list, losing values.
After pop, milli and nano are now empty lists, so `if milli or nano` is falsy and expression.set('sec', sec) is skipped even though sec was modified.
zone.pop() mutates expression.args, causing side effects on the original tree.
The early return triggers for any unit when date_part_boundary is set, casting both operands to DATE. This is only correct for DAY and yields wrong results for other units.
end and start are built as raw SQL strings via f-strings instead of Expression nodes.
self.func is called with the string end/start, so the SQL string is quoted as a literal and DATE_TRUNC receives a string literal instead of a timestamp expression.
When date_part_boundary is truthy the function returns at line 41, so the DATE_TRUNC boundary block is unreachable for that case.
defs[primary_key.expressions[0].name] assumes the column definition exists in defs; missing entry raises KeyError.
column.constraints may be None; enumerating it raises TypeError.

After _match_pair(L_PAREN, VALUES) consumes '(' VALUES, the code tries to match VALUES or FORMAT VALUES again. The second match will almost always fail, so a normal derived VALUES is rejected and the function returns None.

Alias is parsed at line 115 and then parsed a second time in the return expression alias=alias or self._parse_table_alias(). This causes double consumption of the alias token and can skip or corrupt following tokens.
When DEFAULT is matched the value is built as exp.var(self._prev.text.upper()), i.e. a Var node with text 'DEFAULT'. This represents a variable named DEFAULT instead of a proper DEFAULT literal.

The factor from DATE_DIFF_FACTOR is concatenated directly to the SQL string: EXTRACT(epoch FROM ...) ){factor}. Without an explicit operator the output is syntactically invalid unless factor already contains the operator.

When ordinality is present the alias string is moved into the ordinality string and the alias variable is cleared, changing the order of rendering and relying on the alias already containing its separator.
RETURNING is parsed at line 66 and then again in the Insert node as returning or self._parse_returning() at line 97. Parsing twice can consume tokens that belong to the source expression.
Version is concatenated to pre_alias/post_alias without an explicit separator: f"{pre_alias}{version}". If pre_alias is non-empty the version will be glued directly to it.
expression.args.get('laterals') and [] evaluates to [] when laterals is truthy and to None when falsy, so the comprehension never renders laterals and will raise TypeError on None.
alter_token = self._match_set(...) and self._prev can be False when the match fails, but later code accesses alter_token.token_type, causing AttributeError.
Unconditional `if self._next: self._advance()` discards the next token regardless of its type, skipping input that should be parsed for the ALTER statement.
`literal is not False` treats None as valid, so an empty bracket segment is not rejected and can propagate a None into indexes.
When len(indexes)==2 the node is built from indexes[0] only; the second index is ignored, producing incorrect JSONPathKey/Selector/Subscript nodes.
The WHILE condition consumes a COMMA before knowing a mixed action follows. If the following PROPERTY/ALTER checks fail the comma is already lost, corrupting options/cascade parsing.
Unknown unit falls back to `unit=age` producing CAST(interval AS BIGINT) which is invalid Postgres SQL and fails at runtime.
REPLACE token is consumed even when neither WHERE nor USING follows, silently dropping the keyword and accepting invalid syntax.
source uses `_match(TABLE) or _parse_table()` so when TABLE matches it short-circuits to True and never parses the following table, losing the source table.

Exactly-one check uses `bool(vcs_info) - bool(archive_info) + bool(dir_info) != 1`. Subtracting archive_info makes archive_info alone evaluate to -1 and changes the count for all combinations, so valid archive_info cases are rejected and invalid combinations can pass.

license_refs is built from the raw tokens including a trailing '+'. When a LicenseRef token ends with '+', final_token is stripped of '+' before the lookup `license_refs[final_token]`, so the key is missing and a KeyError is raised.

_parse_version_many appends a COMMA token and then loops back without verifying that a SPECIFIER follows. A trailing comma or `,,` is therefore accepted and the comma is returned in parsed_specifiers, violating `SPECIFIER (WS? COMMA WS? SPECIFIER)*`.
alter_token is False/None when _match_set fails, so .token_type raises AttributeError. Same crash repeats at line 31 and line 69.
Unconditionally advances one token if any token remains, consuming the action keyword, then looks up parser via _prev instead of _curr.

Comma is consumed by _match before checking PROPERTY_PARSERS, losing it, and _prev.token_type crashes if _prev is None. Second action keyword is also consumed by _match_texts then re-looked-up via _prev causing double-consume mismatch with first action.
EXTRACT(days FROM interval) returns day-of-month component, not total days, so WEEK diff is wrong for intervals spanning months.
QUARTER uses floating division month/3 then CAST truncates toward zero, giving wrong quarters for negative intervals and fractional months.
Fallback sets unit to AGE() interval then CAST(interval AS BIGINT) which is invalid in Postgres for unhandled units.
Early return for FIRST/ALL discards already-parsed hint, overwrite, ignore, local.
Appends target.this, dropping table qualifier, db, and column metadata from INSERT...SET assignments.
REPLACE token is consumed even when neither WHERE nor USING follows, silently dropping it.
After _match_pair(L_PAREN,VALUES) already consumed VALUES, code requires another VALUES or FORMAT VALUES, and returns None without rewinding, losing consumed tokens.
Always returns a Values expression even when no values parsed, blocking `or _parse_ddl_select()` fallback for INSERT...SELECT.
The DIRECTORY branch parses this but never returns, so execution falls through to SET/RETURNING/INSERT parsing and builds a wrong Insert node.
alternative = self._match_texts(...) and self._prev.text sets alternative to False when the match fails instead of None, breaking the str|None contract.
After consuming '(' VALUES, the code tries to match another VALUES / FORMAT VALUES token and returns None on mismatch, consuming and discarding tokens and incorrectly rejecting valid derived VALUES.
Alias is parsed at line 115 and then parsed again in the Values constructor with alias or self._parse_table_alias(), causing a second consumption of the alias tokens.
parts[2] is accessed without verifying parts has at least 3 elements, which can raise IndexError for malformed aggregate names.

The operator token is advanced with self._advance() and then _parse_string() is called, assuming the current token is the string literal. Kind extraction via partition('_')[2] also mis-handles operators with multiple underscores.
ordinality is set to `expression.args.get('ordinality') and ''`, so a truthy value becomes '' and the following `if ordinality:` never runs. WITH ORDINALITY is therefore never emitted.
When `view` is true the code accesses `expression.args['alias']` directly. Missing alias raises KeyError.
`table_alias` can be None, but `self.sql(table_alias)` is called unconditionally, which can crash.
`expression.this.args.get('offset')` assumes `expression.this` is not None; a missing `this` raises AttributeError.
`defs[primary_key.expressions[0].name]` raises KeyError if the primary key references a column not present in `defs`.

`unit = expression.text('unit').upper() and 'DAY'` uses `and` instead of `or`; any non-empty unit becomes the literal 'DAY', so WEEK/MONTH/etc are never handled and `expression.text` may be None causing AttributeError on `.upper()`.

Alias is parsed at line 115 and then re-parsed with alias or self._parse_table_alias() at line 121. If the first parse returns None the second parse consumes the next tokens, losing the intended alias and advancing the cursor incorrectly.
factor = DATE_DIFF_FACTOR.get(unit) is computed but never used afterwards, so units that require scaling are not scaled and the diff is wrong.

For units not explicitly handled the code sets unit = age, an interval expression, and returns CAST(unit AS BIGINT). Casting an interval to BIGINT is invalid in Postgres and yields wrong results for DAY, HOUR, MINUTE, SECOND, etc.

RETURNING is parsed once at line 66 before the source and again with returning or self._parse_returning() at line 97. The double parse can consume tokens twice or miss a RETURNING that appears after the source.
source=self._match(TokenType.TABLE) and self._parse_table() matches TABLE again after TABLE was already consumed at line 29, so the source table is mis-parsed or skipped.
ordinality is set to expression.args.get('ordinality') and "" which becomes "" when present, so the subsequent `if ordinality:` is always false and WITH ORDINALITY is never emitted.
When view is present the code does expression.args["alias"] without checking existence, raising KeyError if alias is missing.
expression.this may be None, so expression.this.args.get('offset') raises AttributeError.
super()._parse_function can return None, but expr.this is accessed unconditionally, causing AttributeError.
milli.pop() mutates the original expression args and sec is an Expression, so sec += milli.pop() / ... mixes Expression with float and corrupts the tree.
nano.pop() similarly mutates the node and adds a float to an Expression, leading to type errors and lost nano data; expression.set('sec', sec) stores a mixed type.
Auto-increment is inserted at primary_key_index, placing it before the primary key constraint. Docstring requires auto_increment after primary key.
defs[primary_key.expressions[0].name] will raise KeyError if the primary key references a column not present in schema.expressions, e.g., a missing column definition.
paths = expression.expressions is evaluated before confirming expression is a JSONExtract, so an expression without expressions attribute can raise AttributeError.

exp.Array(expressions=[expression.expression, *paths]) uses expression.expression which is not the first path; paths already contains all paths, leading to duplication or AttributeError and wrong SQL.
Early return for JSONExtract bypasses the wrapping logic applied to arrow_sql, breaking the same_parent / WRAPPED_JSON_EXTRACT_EXPRESSIONS contract.
Condition `literal is not False` uses identity check and treats None as valid, allowing empty segments to pass and later cause errors.
Appending is guarded by `if literal:`, which discards falsy but valid indexes such as 0 or empty string.
For len(indexes)==2 the node is built from indexes[0] while the type decision is based on the last parsed literal. The second index is ignored, producing wrong JSONPathKey/Selector/Subscript nodes.
expr returned by super()._parse_function can be None. The code unconditionally accesses expr.this, which raises AttributeError and crashes the parser.

After matching USING ANALYZER the code parses an analyzer name and then raises an error if analyzer is truthy. The condition is inverted, so an error is raised when a name is present and no error is raised when it is missing.
Analyzer validation is inverted: an error is raised when an analyzer name is successfully parsed and no error is raised when it is missing.

Laterals are iterated with `expression.args.get('laterals') and []`. When laterals is missing the expression evaluates to None and the comprehension raises TypeError; when present it always iterates over an empty list, so laterals are never emitted.
The advance is performed unconditionally whenever a next token exists, discarding a token that belongs to the ALTER action. This causes skipped input and incorrect parsing.
An Alter node is only returned when self._curr is falsy. If any token remains, the successfully parsed Alter is discarded and the input is reparsed as a command.
The factor is concatenated directly to the EXTRACT expression without an operator/space, producing invalid SQL like EXTRACT(...)123.
PostgreSQL EXTRACT expects singular unit names; EXTRACT(days FROM ...) is invalid, the correct unit is day.
For unsupported units the code falls back to AGE(...) and then CASTs the interval to BIGINT, which is invalid SQL in Postgres.
self._match(TokenType.TABLE) returns a bool, so source becomes True instead of a parsed table expression when the keyword is present.
RETURNING is parsed at line 184 and then parsed again here with `returning or self._parse_returning()`, causing double consumption.
For derived VALUES the alias is parsed before the closing parenthesis is consumed, so the alias can be taken from inside the value list and the closing paren is matched too late.
When alias is None the code calls self._parse_table_alias() a second time, consuming input twice and potentially skipping tokens.
INSERT ... SET normalization wraps the target table in exp.Schema(this=this, expressions=columns), losing the original table node and breaking the Insert contract.
alter_token is set with `and self._prev` so it can be False; subsequent accesses to alter_token.token_type at lines 25 and 31 will raise AttributeError when the ALTERABLE match fails.
Unconditional `if self._next: self._advance()` skips the next token unconditionally, discarding the ALTER action keyword and corrupting the parse state.
While condition accesses `self._prev.token_type` without checking that `self._prev` is not None, which can crash when the parser is at start of input.
Inside the mixed-actions loop `self.ALTER_PARSERS[self._prev.text.upper()]` is accessed without verifying `self._prev` exists or that the text is a valid key, leading to AttributeError/KeyError.
An ALTER node is only returned when `not self._curr` is true; any remaining tokens cause the method to fall through to `_parse_as_command`, turning valid ALTER statements into commands.
Factor is concatenated directly to the EXTRACT expression `...){factor}` with no separator, producing invalid SQL unless factor already contains leading whitespace.
For units not handled explicitly the code sets `unit = age` and returns `CAST(AGE(...) AS BIGINT)`, which is invalid Postgres SQL and yields wrong results.
When DEFAULT is matched the parser creates `exp.var(self._prev.text.upper())` i.e., a var node named 'DEFAULT' instead of a proper DEFAULT marker/value.

`_parse_derived_table_values` consumes '(' VALUES via `_match_pair` then immediately tests for another VALUES with `_match_text_seq`, which will never succeed, causing the function to return None for all derived VALUES parses.
Alias is parsed twice: once into `alias` and again as `alias or self._parse_table_alias()`, potentially consuming an extra token and losing the first alias.
